items.content:
마크 저커버그 메타 CEO가 마침내 최첨단 AI 모델 경쟁에 복귀했다며 자신감을 드러냈습니다. 지난해 4월 '라마 4'의 실패 이후 AI 조직을 전면 개편하고 막대한 자금을 투입한 지 약 1년 반 만입니다. 이제는 경쟁사를 따라잡는 단계를 넘어, 개인용 초지능 시장에서 차별화하겠다는 구상입니다.

메타가 12일(현지시간) 공개한 ' 뮤즈 원더(Muse Wonder) '는 독립 평가기관 아티피셜 애널리시스의 지능 지수(AAII)에서 앤트로픽에 이어 2위권에 올랐습니다. 특히 고성능 버전인 '뮤즈 원더 풀'은 현재 1위 모델인 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'에 근접한 성능을 기록했습니다. 공식 발표에서도 최첨단 수준의 모델을 확보했다는 점을 전면에 내세웠습니다.

저커버그는 이날 공개된 유튜브 '치키 파인트' 인터뷰에서 "우리는 이번 모델이 상당히 자랑스럽다"라며 "라마 4의 개발 방향에 만족하지 못했다는 것은 잘 알려진 사실이다. 그래서 팀 전체를 사실상 다시 구축했다. 지난 1년 반 동안 엄청난 일이 있었다"라고 말했습니다.

또 "이제 최첨단 수준에 도달했기 때문에 앞으로 우리가 하는 모든 일은 그 경계를 더 넓히는 작업이 될 것"이라며, 그동안은 이 수준에 도달하기 위한 기초 작업이 필요했다고 설명했습니다.

파이낸셜타임스(FT) 인터뷰 에서도 "여기까지 오는 데는 막대한 연산 자원과 투자, 그리고 오랜 기간에 걸친 치밀한 과학적 연구가 필요했다"라고 강조했습니다. 이미 차세대 모델 개발에 착수했다며 앞으로는 개발 속도가 상당히 빨라질 것이라는 자신감도 드러냈습니다.

실제로 메타는 지난해 라마 4가 기대에 미치지 못하자 거액을 들여 알렉산드르 왕 등 핵심 인재를 영입하고 AI 연구 조직을 전면 재편했습니다. 당초 기대했던 것보다 성과가 늦어졌지만, 이번에야 비로소 대규모 투자의 결과를 보여준 셈입니다.

여기에 저커버그는 지난해부터 모든 사람에게 개인용 초지능을 제공하겠다는 구상을 경쟁사와의 차별점으로 내세워 왔습니다. 이제야 이를 뒷받침할 최첨단 모델을 확보하게 된 것입니다.

FT 인터뷰에서도 이런 점이 강조됐습니다. 그는 "다른 기업들은 지식 노동과 자동화에 집중하고 있지만, 우리는 개인의 역량을 강화하는 데 훨씬 더 집중하고 있다"라고 말했습니다.

최근 미국에서 인기를 얻고 있는 개인용 AI 에이전트 '뮤즈(Muse)'가 그 출발점입니다. 메타는 뮤즈 원더를 뮤즈에 적용해 단순한 질의응답을 넘어 구매와 예약, 정보 분석 등 개인의 일상적인 업무를 처리하는 능력을 강화할 계획입니다.

왕 메타 최고 AI책임자(CAIO)도 "지금이 중요한 순간"이라며 "업계 대부분이 코딩 에이전트에 집중해 왔지만, 우리는 개인용 에이전트의 활용 경험을 높이는 데 차별화된 초점을 맞췄다"라고 강조했습니다.

특히 이번 모델에는 사용자의 정보를 대화가 바뀌어도 기억하는 '액티브 메모리'와 작업 중 문제가 발생해도 다른 방법을 시도하며 목표를 계속 추구하는 '액티브 포커스'가 도입됐습니다. 왕은 이러한 기능을 통해 개인용 AI가 더 복잡하고 모호한 업무까지 처리할 수 있을 것으로 기대했습니다.

나아가 저커버그는 현재 AI의 한계도 지적했습니다. 그는 "AI가 고급 수학 문제를 해결하는 수준에 도달했는데도 모든 사람을 위한 고객 지원조차 안정적으로 처리하지 못한다는 것이 어떤 의미인지 모르겠다"라며 여전히 해결할 과제가 많다고 말했습니다.

결국 이번 발표는 메타가 최첨단 모델 경쟁에서 다시 출발선에 섰다는 선언에 가깝습니다. 지난 1년 반 동안은 경쟁사를 따라잡는 데 집중했다면, 이제는 이미 소비자 시장에서 성과를 보이고 있는 뮤즈를 앞세워 개인용 AI의 활용 범위를 넓히겠다는 것입니다.

다만 최첨단 모델 경쟁에 복귀한 것과 개인용 초지능을 실현하는 것은 별개로, 이제 메타는 그동안 내세운 비전을 실제 제품으로 증명해야 하는 단계에 들어섰습니다.

■ 국감서 "AI 캐릭터 챗봇, 청소년 보호 구멍" 지적...규제 급물살 타나

국정감사에서 스캐터랩의 '제타'가 청소년 보호 모드에서도 유해 콘텐츠를 생성하고 안전장치까지 우회하는 문제가 지적됐습니다. 이에 업체들은 이용 시간과 결제 한도 제한 등 대응책을 내놓고 있으며, 정부도 관련 규제의 법제화를 검토하겠다고 밝혔습니다.

한 개발자가 클로드를 활용해 포토샵과 일러스트레이터, 프리미어 프로 등 어도비의 주요 제품을 모방한 무료 오픈소스 소프트웨어 '아트크래프트'를 공개했습니다. AI를 활용하면 기존 소프트웨어를 빠르게 복제할 수 있다는 가능성을 보여줬지만, 저작권 문제와 실제 완성도를 둘러싼 논란도 커지고 있습니다.

■ "말 한마디로 3D 기계 그려내"...클로드 코드용 '아나토미' 공개

한 개발자가 간단한 문장만 입력하면 기계의 구조와 작동 원리를 움직이는 입체 시각화로 구현하는 오픈소스 스킬 '아나토미'를 공개했습니다. AI 코딩 도구가 단순한 프로그램 제작을 넘어 복잡한 기술 개념을 시각적으로 설명하는 교육 도구로도 발전할 수 있다는 점에서 주목됩니다.

items.content:
구글이 플래그십 모델 ‘제미나이 4 아르곤(Gemini 4 Argon)’을 전 세계 개발자와 기업, 유료 이용자에게 확대 출시했다. 지난달 제한적으로 공개한 모델을 본격 상용화하면서, 복잡한 실제 업무에서 거둔 성과와 기존 제품에 통합하는 전략을 전면에 내세웠다.

구글은 13일(현지시간) 아르곤을 구글 AI 스튜디오와 제미나이 플랫폼 API로 제공한다고 발표했다. 구글 AI 프로·울트라 구독자는 제미나이 앱과 검색의 AI 모드에서, 울트라 구독자는 코딩 도구 ‘안티그래비티’에서도 이용할 수 있다.

지난 9월30일 일부 사이버보안 파트너를 대상으로 처음 공개한 지 13일 만이다. 당시에는 모델의 추론 능력과 단계적인 공개 방침을 강조했다면, 이번 발표에서는 기업과 개발자가 실제로 어떤 일을 맡길 수 있는지에 초점을 맞췄다.

코라이 카부쿠오글루 구글 딥마인드 수석 부사장은 “아르곤은 코딩, 금융, 법률, 사이버보안, 과학 등 다양한 영역에서 복잡하고 실제적인 작업을 심층적으로 처리하는 데 탁월하다”라고 강조했다.

여러 문서와 도구를 오가며 장시간 수행하는 업무에서 아르곤이 맥락을 유지하고 분석과 실행을 이어갈 수 있다고 설명했다. 코드 생성뿐 아니라 기존 시스템을 조사하고, 수정한 결과를 시험하는 능력을 주요 경쟁력으로 제시했다.

대표적인 사례는 구글의 오픈소스 에이전트 개발 키트(ADK) 최적화다. 별도의 기술 발표 를 통해 약 800개 소스 파일, 20만5000줄 규모의 파이썬 코드베이스에서 아르곤이 성능 병목을 찾아 수정한 과정을 공개했다.

팀의 유지보수 지침과 목표를 제공받은 아르곤은 안티그래비티에서 11시간 동안 무인으로 작업했다. 공개 단위 테스트 1만6892개를 실행하고, 32개 파일에 걸친 6개 최적화 제안을 제출했다.

다만 제안이 모두 배포된 것은 아니다. 개발팀은 코드 검토를 거쳐 세션 복사와 패키지 지연 로딩에 관한 2개 최적화를 채택했다. 나머지 4개는 오래된 데이터를 반환할 위험, 라이브러리의 비공개 구현에 대한 의존, 실질적인 효과 없이 복잡성을 높이는 문제 등으로 제외했다.

공개 테스트를 모두 통과한 변경에서도 구글 내부 테스트와의 호환성 문제가 발견돼 수정이 필요했다. 자율 실행으로 변경안을 만드는 능력과 실제 배포 여부를 판단하는 작업이 구분된 사례다. 구글 개발팀은 “에이전트는 탐색을 담당하고, 유지 관리자는 불필요한 부분을 제거한다”라고 설명했다.

아르곤을 활용해 20만 줄이 넘는 파이썬 코드베이스를 최적화한 결과, 성능 향상을 보여주는 5가지 벤치마크 (사진=구글)

최종 반영된 변경으로 긴 세션의 메모리 내 세션 준비 시간은 약 40% 줄었으며, 패키지 로딩 속도는 21% 개선됐다. 이는 ADK 전체나 AI 응답 속도가 같은 비율로 빨라졌다는 의미는 아니다. 새 프로세스에서 첫 모델 요청까지 걸리는 시간은 거의 변하지 않았다.

구글은 더 넓은 내부 개발 성과도 제시했다. 안티그래비티에서 아르곤을 사용하는 엔지니어링 팀은 에이전트 기반 코드 제출이 35% 이상 늘었으며, 코드 변경을 되돌리는 롤백은 약 3분의 1 감소했다고 밝혔다. 크롬 팀에서는 수백 개 파일에 걸친 구조 개편을 지원해 수개월이 걸릴 것으로 예상한 작업을 수주 만에 완료했다고 설명했다.

초기 참여 기업으로는 딜로이트와 렉시스넥시스, 앰비언스 헬스케어, 아이소모픽 랩스 등이 있다. 렉시스넥시스는 법률 근거 확인과 계약 검토, 소송 분석에서 긍정적인 결과를 보고했다. 아이소모픽 랩스는 복잡한 PDF와 특허에서 정보를 추출하는 데 아르곤을 활용해 신약 연구 업무를 가속하고 있다고 밝혔다.

외부 전문가의 평가는 신중했다. 기업용 AI 컨설팅·교육 회사 레드 드래곤 AI의 공동 창립자 겸 CEO인 샘 위테빈은 사전 영상 리뷰에서 아르곤을 “정말, 정말, 정말 좋은 모델”이라고 평가하면서도, 시중 최고의 모델인지에 대해서는 “그렇게 생각하지는 않는다”라고 말했다.

또 시각적 이해와 코드 생성, 창의적인 제작을 결합한 작업에서 아르곤의 강점이 두드러진다고 평가했다. 하지만 “여전히 안티그래비티가 클로드 코드나 코덱스만큼 훌륭하다고 생각하지 않는다”라며, 기본 모델과 이를 활용하는 개발 도구의 완성도를 구분했다.

구글은 초기 도입을 촉진하기 위해 한시적인 할인 요금도 마련했다. 오는 11월30일까지 API 가격은 입력 100만 토큰당 2달러, 출력 100만 토큰당 10달러다. 12월1일부터는 각각 4달러와 20달러로 인상된다. 캐시된 입력에는 95% 할인을 적용한다.

연구자 확보를 위해 자격 요건과 선정 기준에 따라 과학자 1만명에게 안티그래비티의 최고 사용 등급을 6개월간 무료 제공한다. 검증된 사이버보안 전문가에게 특정 보안 제한을 제거한 모델을 제공하는 ‘페어윈드’ 프로그램도 수백 곳의 추가 파트너로 확대한다.

이번 상용화는 모델 출시 지연과 조직 개편을 겪은 구글의 경쟁력 회복 시험대이기도 하다. 당초 출시 예정이었던 '제미나이 3.5 프로'를 철회했으며, 딥마인드 경영진 변화와 핵심 인력 이탈을 겪었다.

성능도 최고라고 볼 수는 없다. 아티피셜 애널리시스 지능 지수(AAII)에서는 앤트로픽과 메타의 첨단 모델에 뒤졌다. 이날 공개된 아레나.ai의 '에이전트 아레나' 종합 순위에서도 5위를 차지했다.

이런 상황에서 구글이 내세우는 강점은 모델을 배포할 수 있는 제품과 인프라다. 클라우드와 제미나이 앱, 검색, 개발 도구에 아르곤을 연결해 기존 고객이 사용하는 환경에서 AI 활용 범위를 넓히는 전략이다.

전문가들도 구글이 모든 평가에서 승리해야 성공하는 것은 아니라는 취지로 평가했다. 기존 고객의 업무에 통합할 수 있을 만큼 발전된 모델을 제공하는 것이 중요하다는 설명이다.

카부쿠오글루는 “아르곤은 시작에 불과하다”라며 “앞으로 제미나이 4 제품군의 나머지 모델들도 선보일 예정”이라고 밝혔다.

Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman thinks the AI doomer narrative isn’t doing the industry any favors. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 , the AI chipmaker exec quipped that “some of the leaders in the AI world maybe shouldn’t be allowed to talk in public.”

He’s referencing the negativity now spreading around the dangers of AI, from models breaking containment to AI insiders debating the percentage chance that AI may kill all of humanity by the end of the decade. The argument has become so mainstream that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was recently parodied in a skit on Saturday Night Live , where the fictional character summed up the discourse, saying, “We do not condone what we are doing.”

Feldman, however, thinks the promise and potential that go hand-in-hand with AI developments are getting overlooked. He thinks AI leaders should spend more time telling people that AI could lead to a world where your grandkids will “never meet anybody who dies of cancer,” for instance, even if they have concerns about AI risks.

Clearly, Feldman has a vested interest in AI being successful, as the company’s customers include big names working with the technology, like OpenAI, Block, Figma, pharmaceutical giant GSK, and Lovable.

However, he’s pragmatic about weighing the tradeoffs between risk and reward.

“I don’t think there are powerful technologies that don’t come with the challenge of ‘what happens when powerful technologies are in the hands of bad people?’ I think you can’t make one and not have the other,” Feldman said during his interview at Disrupt.

“I think what we have to say is that this technology is powerful,” he added. “We have to be thoughtful about it. We have to regulate it reasonably,” he added.

The chipmaker CEO also suggested that some of the negativity around AI has to do with how the data center industry has approached the new buildouts created by AI demand.

“As an industry, we weren’t super good for the past few years at working with local communities, particularly in the U.S. We — the industry — didn’t do what others have done in the power industry in oil and gas. They didn’t work with the community. They didn’t engage the community as they should have, and that was a problem,” Feldman said.

He compared the NIMBY-ism — “not in my back yard!” — of what’s going on in the U.S. with other countries, naming Brazil, Canada, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Mexico, and Sweden as markets where they’re encouraging companies to build data centers.

Feldman also wasn’t concerned that efficiency improvements would create less demand for his chips, or those from other companies competing with Nvidia, as Cerebras is.

“We can do our job as hardware vendors to make our compute more efficient, and then the model makers can do improved work in making their models more efficient to achieve the same goals. All of this has to come together to make meaningful strides forward,” he noted.

items.content:
OpenAI engineer arrested for allegedly planting spy device in office

A Saudi OpenAI engineer has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to secretly record sensitive conversations.

The U.S. Department of Justice announced Tuesday that Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with illegally intercepting oral communications.

The DOJ says OpenAI security personnel discovered the recording device on September 30, plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room.

According to the DOJ, OpenAI determined that the device had been concealed in toilet paper, was installed around September 28, and contained encrypted data.

"On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device (Recording Device 1) inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room inside one of their buildings in San Francisco," says the DOJ press release .

Spy device found in OpenAI executive conference room

The DOJ says the conference room was regularly used for meetings involving confidential information about OpenAI's proprietary research, product plans, technical capabilities, business relationships, and government engagements.

Security camera footage allegedly showed Alfozan near the conference room on multiple occasions, despite not being authorized to attend meetings held there.

According to the complaint, Alfozan also used a productivity tool to search for information about OpenAI's offices, meeting rooms, executive locations, and meeting schedules.

The complaint also says a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse was used to ask questions about building and concealing recording devices.

These included inquiries about creating a continuous audio recorder, modifying Wi-Fi connectivity, improving live listening capabilities, and encrypting an SD card.

"The same chatbot account also submitted prompts specifically related to Recording Device 1, including its custom header and unique MAC address, between Sept. 27 and Sept. 28," alleges the DOJ.

On October 5, surveillance footage allegedly captured Alfozan returning to the conference room and looking behind the television where the device had been installed.

The complaint says that on that same day, OpenAI security employees discovered a second, similar recording device inside a bag Alfozan had left unattended in another room.

In a statement posted on X, OpenAI said it used its own AI models to investigate the suspicious device and help identify the employee responsible.

"We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier," OpenAI said.

The company said it terminated the employee and referred the incident to the FBI.

"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI added.

If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

뉴욕증시는 중국 반도체 기업의 기술 발전에 따른 경쟁 심화 우려와 투자자 기대에 못 미친 대형 은행의 실적 발표에 일제히 하락 마감했다.

13일(현지시간) 뉴욕증권거래소(NYSE)에서 다우존스30 산업평균지수는 전장 대비 180.45포인트(0.35%) 하락한 5만1670.10에 거래를 마쳤다.

스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500지수는 1.79포인트(0.02%) 내린 7,805.45에, 기술주 중심의 나스닥종합지수는 41.52포인트(0.15%) 떨어진 2만7204.38에 거래를 마쳤다.

필라델피아반도체지수는 0.23% 하락하며 5거래일 연속 내렸다. 반도체 업종은 중국 반도체 기업의 기술 발전에 따른 경쟁 심화 우려에 약세를 보였다.

전날 중국 창신메모리(CXMT)는 D램 메모리 기술에서 새로운 진전을 이뤘다며 올해 안에 이를 이용한 차세대 서버용 제품을 선보일 계획이라고 밝혔다.

종목별로는 마이크론테크놀로지(3.62%), 어플라이드머티어리얼즈(6.69%) 등이 급락했다. 다만 엔비디아(0.97%), 인텔(1.44%) 등은 상승하며 엇갈린 흐름을 나타냈다.

본격적인 3분기 실적 발표 시즌이 시작된 가운데 대형 은행의 실적이 투자자 기대에 못 미치면서 주가가 약세를 보였다.

씨티그룹(5.6%)과 웰스파고(3.1%), 골드만삭스(0.2%) 등 대형 은행은 지난해보다 증가한 순이익을 발표했음에도 주가가 하락했다.

월서 웰스 매니지먼트의 레베카 월서 최고투자책임자(CIO)는 "은행들은 여전히 견조한 실적을 발표했지만, 기대치가 너무 높았다"고 평가했다.

국제유가는 혼조세를 보였다. 미국과 러시아 간 경유 거래 합의에 따른 공급 확대 기대와 중동 지역의 지정학적 긴장이 맞물린 영향으로 풀이된다.

items.summary: Unit 42 dissects a cyberattack targeting a European bank's IT infrastructure, delivering concrete defense strategies to help organizations detect and counter comparable threats. The post The Noise Inside the Network: How an Unsophisticated Attack Exposed a Third-Party Risk appear
items.content:
When unusual activity was detected on a European bank’s central IT system, its internal security team quickly recognized that the incident warranted immediate response. They discovered unauthorized VPN-based access attempts that spanned several months. They then engaged Unit 42 to determine the full scope of the intrusion, identify any persistent footholds and secure the environment.

While the activity appeared to be a stealthy cyberespionage campaign, the actual intrusion was made possible by gaps in foundational security controls. Rather than relying on novel techniques, the threat actor succeeded through persistence, exploiting weaknesses that stronger identity protections and basic security hygiene could have prevented. The case highlights an important lesson: Sometimes the most damaging intrusions begin with the simplest oversights.

The intrusion originated through a third-party-managed external gateway appliance that was not properly configured to enforce strict authentication. Using compromised credentials, the attacker began by authenticating to internal systems. Once inside, the threat actor launched a discovery campaign of the internal network.

The threat actor conducted multiple rounds of reconnaissance, performing extensive host and network scans across a wide range of protocols and interacting with thousands of systems. This broad, noisy approach was less a targeted strike than casting a net to uncover as many access points as possible.

The pattern continued with credential testing. Over a period of a few months, the threat actor launched multiple password-guessing campaigns. They hammered at internal systems with brute-force authentication attempts, focusing on administrator accounts.

While doing this, they systematically targeted internal documentation and data shares. Using automated web requests, they scraped individual pages and attachments from internal systems and enumerated various operational and network shares.

The activity observed did not match the behavior typically associated with a sophisticated threat actor. The noise behind the scanning and login attempts, along with using common system identifiers, pointed to an opportunistic attacker attempting to compromise multiple systems. Their actions showed little effort to remain hidden or avoid detection.

In the final stages, the intruder attempted to expand control by exploiting a Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) remote code execution vulnerability on the central configuration management server. This server handled software distribution across the bank, making it a prime target for privilege escalation and long-term persistence.

However, the attacker's luck ran out. The moment they attempted to execute unauthorized code, Cortex XDR identified the activity and contained the threat before it could escalate. The attacker was prevented from gaining a persistent foothold or moving laterally throughout the network.

When Unit 42 engaged, our team initiated a comprehensive threat-hunting effort. We performed a deep forensic review of endpoint telemetry across approximately thousands of systems, alongside logs from dozens of Windows and Linux servers. Ultimately, no additional attacker presence or persistent backdoors were found. Bank leadership acted quickly to review the exposed documentation and rotate all compromised credentials, completely neutralizing the threat.

This case serves as a critical reminder that not every cyber threat is advanced and multifaceted. Opportunistic actors will gladly take advantage of simple oversight, such as missing multi-factor authentication (MFA) on a VPN or an unpatched edge device, to compromise and break into an environment. That being said, an attacker's lack of sophistication doesn't make them harmless.

BNY, Citadel Securities test tokenized U.S. Treasuries to speed up Wall Street financing
items.content:
BNY, the world’s largest custody bank, and trading giant Citadel Securities said Tuesday they had completed a transaction using tokenized U.S. Treasuries, showing how blockchain technology could help Wall Street move assets between trading and financing more quickly.

The transfer focused on collateral, a key part of financial markets. Banks and trading firms use U.S. government bonds to secure short-term loans and fund trading activity. Moving those bonds between accounts and settlement systems can take time, tying up assets that could otherwise be put to work.

The effort comes as Wall Street explores bringing traditional assets onto blockchains. Firms including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton and JPMorgan have embraced tokenized funds and securities, betting the technology can shorten settlement times, automate processes and make assets easier to move.

The aim of the BNY-Citadel Securities transaction was to demonstrate how tokenized government bonds could move from settlement into financing, potentially allowing firms to reuse collateral sooner and free up cash for other trades.

“Efficient movement of high-quality collateral is fundamental to well-functioning markets,” said Dan Doherty, digital assets operations lead at Citadel Securities, in a statement. He added that reducing delays across the trade lifecycle could improve how institutional markets operate.

BNY said it plans to introduce more digital cash and tokenized deposit capabilities to support blockchain-based settlement and financing.

Meanwhile, the bank said it expects to extend the operating hours of its traditional settlement systems for Federal Reserve-eligible securities and U.S. triparty transactions, aiming to reach European and Asian trading hours next year. Triparty transactions are a form of short-term financing in which a bank manages collateral between borrowers and lenders.

“By using a tokenized representation of a U.S. Treasury across both settlement and financing, we are enabling more connected, efficient and always-on financial system,” said Carolyn Weinberg, chief innovation and market transformation officer at BNY, in a statement.

A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-39919) in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine could allow remote code execution through specially crafted PDF files.

The flaw was discovered on August 23 by researchers at Defiant's platform Wordfence using their Argus AI-powered system.

Ghostscript is a PostScript and PDF interpreter that can render PDFs as images, generate thumbnails for previews, and optimize PDF files by compressing embedded images and removing unnecessary font data.

When generating a PDF thumbnail, WordPress can use the PHP Imagick extension to call ImageMagick, which launches Ghostscript.

A specially crafted PDF file containing a JPEG 2000 image can trigger incorrect handling of low-bit-depth samples and mismatched component resolutions.

Using Argus, the researchers developed two exploits for CVE-2026-39919 that force Ghostscript to write 1,024 bytes into a 256-byte buffer, corrupting nearby memory and leading to unauthenticated remote code execution in a WordPress deployment.

Wordfence focused on WordPress systems, but notes that the flaw affects any online system running Ghostscript 9.21 through 10.07.1 and is exploitable if the payload is adjusted to the environment.

The researchers tested ten Linux environments, including Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, and AlmaLinux, as well as an official WordPress Docker image snapshot, and found that all contained the vulnerable code.

The researchers tested two proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits and found that their ability to trigger the vulnerability depended on the target environment.

In a lab testbed, they executed the exploits 10,240 times against Linux packages but failed to achieve remote code execution. However, they successfully executed code remotely on a purpose-built test server.

The researchers found that modifying the PDF's fonts, language settings, font configuration, and one core system library enabled the exploit to succeed, although not reliably.

In WordPress environments specifically, successful exploitation has four prerequisites:

An attacker can upload a PDF, anonymously or through a low-privileged account.

The site processes that PDF to generate a preview or thumbnail.

The processing chain reaches Ghostscript, with the necessary software and policy settings permitting PDF rendering.

Ghostscript contains the unpatched vulnerable decoding code.

Wordfence noted that stock WordPress does not permit anonymous Media Library uploads.

More generally, any application that renders attacker-supplied PDFs through affected Ghostscript code may expose the flaw, and authentication requirements for exploitation depend on the application.

Artifex, the maintainer of Ghostscript, rolled out a fix on September 8, in version 10.08.0 of the interpreter.

Fixes were also backported to older versions, so users should check the revision details for patch status.

WordPress administrators need to ensure, through their hosting provider, that Ghostscript has been upgraded to version 10.08.0 or later.

If using Docker, it is recommended to rebuild and redeploy with an updated, patched base image.

If unable to upgrade to a fixed Ghostscript release, it is recommended to block PDF uploads to the server or disable PDF rendering in ImageMagick.

Wordfence said it has not seen any in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-39919 yet.

items.content:
"이럴 때 사야 돈 번다던데"…코스피 6000 턱걸이에 증권가 '경고' [분석+]

코스피지수가 13일 장중 폭락한 후 6000선을 가까스로 지켜내며 마감했다. 외국인 매도세가 지속되는 가운데, 삼성전자 의 자사주 매수가 종료되며 증시 하단을 받쳐줄 수급이 약해지자 무너진 것이다. 여의도 증권가에선 증시를 둘러싼 환경의 불확실성이 크고 외국인 수급이 언제 돌아올지 불투명하다는 점에서 신중하게 대응해야 한다는 보수적 관점이 필요하다는 조언이 나온다. 반면 절대적인 주가 수준이 낮기에 저가 매수에 나서볼 만하다는 의견도 만만치 않다.

한국거래소에 따르면 13일 코스피는 348.89포인트(5.46%) 하락한 6035.35에 거래를 마쳤다. 장 초반엔 유가증권시장에서 프로그램 매도 호가 효력 일시정지(매도 사이드카)가 발동됐고, 이후에도 급락세가 진정되지 않아 낙폭이 7.41%에 이르는 5911.11까지 빠지기도 했다.

이날 폭락의 방아쇠를 당긴 건 ‘중국산 반도체’다. 중국 창신메모리반도체(CXMT)가 더블데이타레이트(DDR)5 D램 생산을 위한 기술적 진전을 이뤘다고 주장하면서다. 올해 안에 서버용 제품 출시 계획까지 알려지며 메모리반도체 시장의 공급 부족이 풀릴 것으로 전망되면서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스 의 메모리반도체 부문 수익성이 악화할 가능성이 부각돼 투자심리가 냉각됐다.

최근 들어 코스피가 연일 하락하는 배경으로는 외국인 매도세가 지목된다. 외국인은 올해 들어 이날 정규장 마감 무렵까지 유가증권시장에서 232조7062억원어치 현물주식을 순매도했다.

특히 기업의 실적 개선에도 주가가 급락한다는 점이 문제다. 삼성전자가 사상 처음으로 분기 영업이익이 100조원을 넘어섰고, SK하이닉스의 이익 전망도 상향되고 있는데도 외국인 매도세가 멈추지 않고 있어서다. 김석환 미래에셋증권 연구원은 "현재 시장에서는 실적 개선보다 외국인 매도를 흡수할 신규 매수세의 부족이 더 크게 부각되고 있다"고 진단했다.

외국인의 매물을 받아줄 국내 투자자의 매수 여력마저 제한적이라는 게 더 큰 문제다. 개인투자자는 2024년 7월 이후 약 195조원을 주식시장에 투입했으며, 가계의 유동성 자산도 전년 동기 대비 감소했다고 LS증권은 지적했다. 이 증권사 정다운 연구원은 "국내 기관투자가든, 개인투자자든 매수 여력이 제한적인 상황에서, 외국인의 순매도가 가격 변동폭을 확대하는 양상"이라고 분석했다.

그동안 외국인이 쏟아내는 매물을 받아내던 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 자사주 매입 수급도 약해졌다. 이날 정규장 마감 무렵까지 기타법인은 4557억원어치 주식을 순매수했다. 9월 한 달 동안 기타법인은 3일 하루를 제외한 모든 거래일에 유가증권시장에서 1조6000억~1조7000억원대의 주식 순매수세를 보였다. 하지만 이달 6일 삼성전자의 자사주 매수가 종료되면서 기타법인의 주식 순매수 규모는 7일 6873억원, 8일 7774억원, 12일 6447억원, 13일 4557억원으로 쪼그라들었다.

김석환 미래에셋증권 연구원은 "그동안 외국인의 반도체 매도를 기타법인의 자사주 매입이 상당 부분 흡수하면서 지수 하단을 지지했지만, 매수 주체가 약화된 뒤 동일한 외국인 매도가 더 큰 가격 충격으로 연결될 수 있다"고 분석했다.

KB증권은 코스피가 저가매수 구간에 진입했다고 평가했다. 김민규 KB증권 연구원은 최근 반도체 대형주에 대한 가치 평가 방식이 다시 경기민감주로 되돌아갔다고 가정해도 현재 주가는 저평가 상태라고 분석했다. 코스피 밴드 하단 역시 12개월 선행 주가순자산비율(PBR) 1.1~1.2배를 적용해 5600~6000선을 제시했다.

반면 삼성증권은 외국인 매도와 대외 불확실성이 지속되는 만큼 공격적인 매수는 이르다고 판단했다. 조아인 삼성증권 연구원은 중국의 메모리 기술 추격 우려와 외국인 매도세에 고유가·고금리 부담까지 겹치면서 시장의 변동성이 확대될 수 있다고 봤다. 그러면서 "현시점에서는 공격적인 비중 확대보다는 주요 이벤트의 전개 과정을 확인하면서 단계적으로 대응하는 전략이 적합하다"고 밝혔다.

미래에셋증권도 주가 하락만을 근거로 매수에 나서는 전략에는 부정적인 의견을 내놨다. 외국인 수급이 돌아오는지를 봐야 한다는 것이 이유다. 김석환 연구원은 외국인 매도가 지속되면 기술적 반등이 나타나더라도 상승 추세로 복귀하기까지 상당한 시간이 걸릴 수 있다고 우려했다.

한경우 기자는 한경닷컴에서 주식투자에 대한 기사를 쓰고 있습니다. 개별 종목 분석과 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠에 특히 두각을 나타냅니다.

그는 2014년 농식품 전문 매체에서 기자 생활을 시작했고, 이후 경제매체 산업부로 자리를 옮겨 중화학공업과 해운, 제약·바이오 산업을 출입하며 주요 산업에 대한 이해를 쌓았습니다. 이를 바탕으로 심층적인 종목 분석 기사를 작성하고 있습니다.

‘한경우의 케이스스터디’ 코너에는 주로 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠가 연재되고 있습니다. 에프앤가이드와 코스콤의 데이터 플랫폼을 능숙하게 다루기에 특정 투자지표를 조건 삼아 관심을 가져 볼만한 종목을 선별해 독자들에게 제시합니다.

‘투자톡’ 코너를 통해서는 각 투자 전략을 장기간 시뮬레이션한 백테스트 콘텐츠를 선보이고 있습니다.

외국인이 하루 만에 유가증권시장에서 4조5000억원어치가 넘는 주식을 던지며 이탈했다. 중국 창신메모리테크놀로지(CXMT)가 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 아성을 위협할 수 있다는 관측이 나오자 반도체 호황을 믿고 한국 ...

코스피가 5% 넘게 급락했다. 정규장 개장 후 한시간도 버티지 못하고 유가증권시장에선 프로그램 매도 호가 효력 일시정지(매도 사이드카)가 발동됐고, 장중엔 6000선을 내주고 5900선 초반까지 밀리기도 했다. 종가...

items.title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
items.summary: Anthropic is warning that small AI models could soon be able to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, from Android TV boxes to smart ovens, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads without relying on data centers. [...]
items.content:
Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices

Anthropic is warning that small AI models could soon be able to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, from Android TV boxes to smart ovens, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads without relying on data centers.

The company's experiments showed that models could identify unfamiliar devices, connect them into a network, and prepare them to run an AI model.

Although the researchers successfully distributed the Gemma4-26B-A4B model from Google DeepMind on 15 off-brand Android TV boxes, they did not demonstrate a fully autonomous, self-replicating AI worm running on real IoT hardware.

However, they estimate that smaller models could achieve self-replication by the end of the year if they continue to improve at their historical rate.

“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes,” Anthropic warns .

“ A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days).”

Anthropic ran its replication experiment using cheap Android TV boxes, and the AI models Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-26B-A4B, Llama3.1-8B, Opus 4.8, and GLM-5.2, each assigned a different role.

Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.2 acted as agents tasked with setting up and propagating Llama3.1-8B (inference), while Gemma4-26B-A4B demonstrated that a model could run across 15 Android TV boxes. Opus 4.8 was separately tested as an advisor to Qwen.

The experiment used a simplified setting where the targets exposed unauthenticated ADB access.

The experiments showed that Qwen3.5-9B successfully installed and configured the software needed to run Llama3.1-8B on eight of the nine hardware types tested.

GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in the controlled emulated network in four out of five trials, but the other models failed to complete the full process reliably.

Anthropic observed an improvement in success rate when it retained data from previous attempts, with Qwen3.5-9 B's success rate rising from 45% early on to 84% in later generations.

Using the stronger Opus 4.8 model to assist Qwen in inference produced no measurable improvement.

Based on the results and historical data, Anthropic predicts that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer could reach the necessary capability level by the end of 2026.

On the studied hardware, the inference setup would be a slow process, taking between 28 and 51 hours for Qwen3.5-9B, and 71-150 hours for Gemma4-26B-A4B, giving defenders enough time to detect and respond.

However, this time could shrink with future models, so implementing stronger security measures for IoT may soon become a priority.

Proposed defenses include detecting large model transfers and unusual device-to-device traffic, using honeypots to inspect payloads, quarantining infected subscribers, and improving IoT security defaults.

While Anthropic’s warning is not based on an imminent threat, as their experiment failed to demonstrate full end-to-end worm-creation capability at this stage, even with lowered security settings and explicit propagation goals, the message for better IoT security remains valid.

items.title: Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue
items.summary: More than 40 residences in Texas were the target of a federal operation in September to clamp down on remote worker scams that feed money back to the North Korean regime.
items.content:
Image: Lala Azizli via Unsplash Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue

The Department of Justice disrupted multiple laptop farms across Texas allegedly being used by North Korean nationals to facilitate an IT worker scheme that allows the country to earn millions from U.S. companies.

The laptop farm raids, which were conducted September 21-25, targeted more than 40 residences, the DOJ said.

Law enforcement seized 187 laptops and other devices used by North Koreans. Such schemes have earned millions over the last eight years by tricking U.S. companies into hiring workers remotely into lucrative IT roles through stolen or purchased identities.

Alongside the raids, the DOJ indicted and arrested U.S. nationals Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas. Several Chinese and North Korean nationals also were indicted. The department did not respond to requests for comment about whether the indictments and arrests were linked to the Texas laptop farm raids.

The DOJ indicted Bostelle and Pena on wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft charges, accusing them of being key U.S.-based cogs in the IT worker scheme.

Bostelle and Pena helped a group of North Koreans earn more than $3 million from about 70 U.S. companies across 17 states, prosecutors said, including organizations in healthcare, cybersecurity, retail and manufacturing.

Large parts of the indictment are centered around U.S. national Trey Michael Nolte, who was not charged.

The DOJ did not explain why he was not charged, but prosecutors said he ran a shell company that facilitated the scheme. Nolte allegedly communicated with Chinese and North Korean nationals, recruited Bostelle, sent packages to China, received work laptops from U.S. companies and laundered the paychecks earned by the IT workers back to North Korea.

From 2019 to 2026, Bostelle and Pena hosted laptops as part of the scheme while also helping IT workers obtain and use fake identification documents to obtain employment or verify bank accounts, prosecutors said

“North Korea’s rogue regime uses its pervasive IT worker schemes to raise revenue for various illicit purposes, including the development of weapons that could ultimately target the United States or its allies,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg.

“These schemes threaten the security of the IT systems and data of the deceived U.S. employers and leave countless victims of identity theft.”

The actions outlined on Tuesday are part of a long-running operation to disrupt laptop farms across the U.S. as well as identify American co-conspirators who sell their identities for use or host laptop farms at their properties.

Nearly 30 laptop farms across 16 states were raided last year by U.S. law enforcement.

Several Americans have already been convicted and sentenced to years in prison for running laptop farms and coordinating with North Koreans on the IT worker scheme.

North Korean nationals funnel the money earned from high-paying IT roles into the country’s government.

Researchers have said several government agencies effectively fund themselves by employing their own coterie of IT workers. Many IT workers are located in China or Russia but a recent United Nations report found hundreds of North Korean IT workers in Laos, Cambodia and several other countries.

Assistant FBI Director Brett Leatherman said North Korea “continues to deploy remote IT workers using stolen identities to infiltrate American companies and generate revenue for the regime and its weapons programs.”

Leatherman noted that the FBI released a new public service announcement describing the latest tactics used by North Korean IT workers to recruit Americans and perpetrate the scheme.

items.content:
Microsoft Patch Tuesday for October 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities

Microsoft has released its monthly security update for October 2026, which includes 1415 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 85 that Microsoft marked as "critical."

Microsoft notes that 1 of the vulnerabilities disclosed this month have been exploited in the wild

CVE-2026-96951 is a security feature bypass vulnerability that affects Windows Shell. The shared weakness is Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection'). The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.8.

Out of 85 "critical" vulnerabilities, 67 are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.

Microsoft considers exploitation of the following vulnerabilities more likely.

CVE-2026-70229 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Windows Active Directory Domain Services. The shared weakness is Incorrect Authorization. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.1.

CVE-2026-70571 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Microsoft Exchange Server. The shared weakness is Stack-based Buffer Overflow. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.1.

Microsoft considers exploitation of the following vulnerabilities less likely.

CVE-2026-105733 , CVE-2026-102214 , and CVE-2026-108399 affect Windows Hyper-V. CVE-2026-105733 has an impact of remote code execution; involves Incorrect Initialization of Resource; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-102214 has an impact of remote code execution; involves Use After Free; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.

Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.

These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.

The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.

The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.

In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data.

Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations.

U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. But he did rule that Apple could access the interview materials, alongside private LINE messages (from a messaging app) between individuals named in the case, including OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng.

The judge also approved depositions for Liu and Peng, along with a third individual, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Yew Tan. All three are former Apple employees.

However, the judge denied Apple’s request to expedite its access to OpenAI’s research and development in specific areas, like metal finishes and power management. He also denied several of Apple’s broader discovery requests, like access to OpenAI’s hardware research or information about what its former employees created while working at OpenAI.

That denial isn’t final, though; the judge left the door open for Apple to narrow its requests and try again.

items.title: FTC: Company netted at least $60 million charging sextortion victims for help it didn’t provide
items.summary: An Ohio-based company charged individuals thousands of dollars to fight sextortion scams, but the operation itself was fraudulent, according to a Federal Trade Commission complaint.
items.content:
Image: Pablo Merchán Montes via Unsplash FTC: Company netted at least $60 million charging sextortion victims for help it didn’t provide

An Ohio-based company allegedly collected at least $60 million by tricking panicked customers facing sextortion threats into buying help the firm didn’t provide, according to a Federal Trade Commission (FTC)  complaint  filed Tuesday.

Digital Forensics Corporation (DFC), owner Dmitry Belkin and several affiliated companies are behind the scheme, which allegedly ran from February 2023 through July 2026, the FTC said. A federal court has temporarily ordered the “sextortion assistance” company from doing business until a decision is reached, the agency said.

Desperate defendants receiving threats from sextortionists who said they will share naked photos or other sensitive sexual information with family members and employers have turned to DFC for help only to be manipulated into spending thousands, the FTC said in a press release .

The company would lure victims into paying between $1,499 and $20,000 in exchange for so-called Phase 1 services that it claimed included stopping the attack, pinpointing the sextortionist’s location with a “tracking campaign,” providing a detailed investigative report, notifying law enforcement and sending a cease-and-desist letter, the complaint said.

In reality, DFC did none of these things, according to the FTC.

“Instead of communicating with the sextortionist through the victim's account, defendants routinely change the victim's account settings simply to block the sextortionist's communications,” the complaint said. “Instead of obtaining investigative information, defendants fabricate chat transcripts.”

DFC also allegedly routinely reused pre-saved location coordinates — typically for Nigeria and the Philippines — to trick customers into believing they had located the sextortionist.

The company used a script for sales calls, the complaint said, and would customize language to play to specific fears different victims might have. For example, victims in the military would be told they could face a dishonorable discharge while married victims were warned that a sextortionist could target their spouses and in-laws, the complaint said.

“Defendants falsely portray themselves as digital forensics experts, claiming they

can track and identify sextortionists, prevent the spread of explicit material and coordinate with

law enforcement to bring criminals to justice,” the complaint said.

DFC staffers allegedly told victims law enforcement would not assist them. The FBI has long recommended that victims ignore and block sextortionists, the complaint said, but the company’s workers would tell customers that doing so is “the last thing you want to do,” according to the complaint.

The company additionally peddled "Phase 2" services for victims willing to pay thousands of dollars more, the complaint said.

While telling victims they only offered Phase 2 in rare cases, the complaint alleged that every customer was pressured into buying the second round of assistance, which purported to include ongoing monitoring of customer accounts, as well as the entire web, to defend against further attacks, the complaint said.

Many customers complained to DFC, citing a contractual refund policy, but the company often would not honor it, the complaint said.

Additionally, the firm allegedly used fake positive reviews while censoring negative reviews, according to the complaint. Upset customers would allegedly be given fake Better Business Bureau websites to complain to.

The firm also allegedly told customers they would not receive partial refunds unless they removed negative reviews. It purchased positive phony reviews by “paying Uber drivers to

post fabricated testimonials using staged photos,” the complaint said.

The FTC said it has received hundreds of reports about DFC’s business practices.

DFC did not respond to a request for comment.

Microsoft classifies a zero-day flaw as publicly disclosed or actively exploited when no official fix is available.

items.title: Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours
items.summary: Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.
items.content:
Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.

Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.

According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.

Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.

The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours.

The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data . A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.

Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules

The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.

SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.

Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.

Microsoft no longer releases new features for Windows 10, and the KB5126657 update mainly includes security updates and bug fixes.

The update also includes fixes released as part of today's record-breaking October 2026 Patch Tuesday, which fixed a massive 1,411 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively exploited zero-day flaw.

The complete list of fixes and changes in KB5126657 is listed below:

This update enables permanent Daylight Savings Time (DST) support for British Columbia and Alberta starting in November 2026.

This update introduces the new time zone Manitoba Standard Time "(UTC-5:00) Manitoba".

[ReFS security] This update adds auditing and optional policy controls for ReFS volumes on externally attached storage devices. Auditing is enabled by default, while enforcement controls remain disabled by default to give administrators time to evaluate and prepare for future security hardening changes. To learn more, see KB5130741 .

[Storage Spaces] Addresses an issue that might cause some Storage Spaces Direct virtual disks to remain offline after installing a Windows update. This issue occurs when valid tiered storage metadata is incorrectly identified as invalid during recovery, preventing affected virtual disks and dependent workloads from coming online.

[File History (known issue)] Fixed: This update addresses an issue where File History might fail to back up or restore files to an external drive or network location. Affected devices might incorrectly display a "Reconnect your drive" message even when a compatible backup drive is connected and working properly.

[Secure Boot] This update continues the deployment of updated Secure Boot certificates using the latest high-confidence targeting data to identify eligible devices that are ready to automatically receive the new certificates. Deployment through Windows Update remains ongoing across supported device.

Microsoft says the update has a known issue affecting some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices after installing the September 2026 Windows security updates.

Affected devices may fail to start with a Code 10 error in Device Manager, stop producing audio, or experience unresponsive volume controls and sound settings. Some devices may also work in standard stereo mode but fail when using 8-channel or 3D audio configurations.

Microsoft partially fixed the issue in an emergency out-of-band update released on September 14, which addressed problems with 8-channel and 3D audio modes.

items.content:
Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely

Learn more about our approach to safety and security for Gemini 4 Argon.

Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMind

Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program , while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google.

This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process.

Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly , as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions:

How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? ( Misuse )

Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? ( Misalignment and Prompt Injection )

Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses. Below are some highlights from how we approached these two questions for Gemini 4 Argon.

Misuse prevention across high-risk domains

The same coding and reasoning improvements that enabled Argon to find and patch vulnerabilities also drove better performance on our cybersecurity tests — solving all 12 of the end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from five in our previous generation. In biology evaluations, unguarded versions of the model also showed a much stronger ability to help troubleshoot complex lab procedures step by step. Following our Frontier Safety Framework , since we saw elevated capabilities in the cyber and biological domains, we put our next-generation set of frontier safeguards in place across both areas.

First, when it comes to potentially dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials, Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly twofold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models. Second, we wrap the model in three layers of real-time protection; this is to prevent determined attackers that might try to jailbreak (i.e. trick) the model by disguising a dangerous request as a harmless story or breaking it into dozens of small questions over several weeks. Here is how these protections work:

Input screening: Smaller models check incoming requests and conversation context for malicious intent or dangerous requests.

Internal introspection: Even if a request is cleverly disguised to look harmless, small transformers ("activation probes") read the model’s internal neural signals and are trained to spot when it is activating knowledge about cyberattacks or biological threats.

Continuous monitoring: As the model reasons and writes its response across multiple steps, we combine these signals and take action when necessary such as cutting off the agent mid-stream if the responses become problematic.

items.title: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
items.summary: CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.
items.content:
CCO Danny Sanders said he had notified certain hardware wallet resellers that they would be removed from Trezor’s list of authorized entities starting Jan. 1.

Hardware wallet producer Trezor announced it would reduce its number of resellers as a “preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution,” following reports that malicious implants had been installed in devices made by competitor Ledger.

In a Tuesday X post, Trezor said there was “not a single piece of evidence that [its] devices have been compromised” after reports that Ledger hardware wallet users had found malicious implants that exposed recovery phrases.

However, Trezor said that it would reduce the number of its resellers, citing “recent supply-chain incidents.” Chief commercial officer Danny Sanders added that he had notified certain resellers that they would be removed from the company’s list of authorized entities on Jan. 1, and would halt shipments of Trezor devices starting on Tuesday.

Trezor’s response came just days after Ledger confirmed that at least one of its devices purchased by a Southeast Asian reseller contained an unauthorized hardware implant, potentially leading to millions of dollars in losses for users. The wallets, sold by reseller CryptoBilis, captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks.

“Our setup checks are built to catch counterfeit devices and modified firmware,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph. “The implant found in a device bought from CryptoBilis works differently. This is a unique way of tampering with the device, which doesn’t modify the firmware, but reads information on the screen and later sends it to the attacker. So far, we have not seen this specific type of attack on Trezor devices in the real world.”

Related: Ledger investigates fund losses linked to Southeast Asian reseller, warns users

During the investigation, CryptoBilis, an authorized Trezor reseller, suspended all hardware wallet sales. The parent company of European electronics retailer MediaMarkt also announced that it had removed all Ledger products from its physical stores and online platforms “as a precautionary measure.”

Blockchain sleuths are still investigating the extent of losses for hardware wallet users, but research from two individuals suggested between $72 million and $86 million. Ledger reported on Tuesday that it had “not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost” due to the breaches.

The Trezor spokesperson advised users to buy products directly from the company, “checking the seal is intact,” and consider a multisignature wallet “with devices from different makers, so one compromised device can’t move funds on its own.”

Microsoft: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of support

Microsoft announced today that devices running Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro editions have reached the end of support and will no longer receive monthly security and non-security preview updates.

However, according to Microsoft's lifecycle policy, Windows 11 24H2 Enterprise and Education editions remain under mainstream support until October 12, 2027.

"Today, October 13, 2026, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 have reached end of updates. The October 2026 monthly security update is the last update available for these editions," Microsoft said in a message center update.

"Devices running these editions will no longer receive monthly security and non-security preview updates containing protections from the latest security threats."

Microsoft advises users to upgrade to Windows 11 26H2, the latest Windows 11 version, also known as the Windows 11 2026 Update, which is now rolling out in phases to eligible Windows 11 devices where the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option has been enabled.

Windows 11 26H2 became generally available in September 2026 as an enablement package and will reach end of support for consumers in October 2029.

items.title: 406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately
items.summary: 406 scientists, including Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, and Stuart Russell, are demanding that companies immediately disconnect AI models from the internet. Their open letter responds to incidents where AI systems broke out of poorly secured environments and compromised externa
items.content:
406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

An open letter signed by 406 scientists calls for more AI safety research and stricter isolation of AI models from external networks.

Among the signatories are prominent AI researchers like Geoffrey Hinton (University of Toronto), Yoshua Bengio (Université de Montréal), Stuart Russell (UC Berkeley), Yejin Choi (Stanford), and Bernhard Schölkopf (Max Planck Institute).

The letter responds to known incidents where AI models broke out of poorly secured environments and compromised external systems. "Without immediate changes in AI development and deployment practices, such incidents will continue to occur, and future incidents will be far more damaging to our exposed critical infrastructure," the scientists write. They demand that companies fully disconnect their AI models from the internet through airgapping. Ad

AI models are unpredictable, and the industry lacks basic safety rules

The scientists see two sides to the recent breaches. The incidents can be viewed "as evidence for the importance of AI alignment to ensure models operate predictably," they write, but also "as an irresponsible lapse in standard cybersecurity practices, preventable with stronger sandboxes and procedures." Both fixes are needed. Ad

When models do have internet access, companies need to weigh how much autonomy to grant them. The letter warns that "the range of model actions permitted by a containment system needs to be balanced with our currently limited ability to predict that the model's actions will not result in a security failure." A model might simply pursue goals its developers never intended, and predicting when that happens remains beyond current capabilities.

The letter calls for an international body that works with governments and specialists from both AI and cybersecurity to set binding standards for any containment approach that allows more external access than airgapping. This body would also track breakout incidents and require companies to report security failures. Those reports would later be made public "for both learning and accountability purposes." Ad

Airgapping buys time, but the real problem runs deeper, OpenAI researcher Brown says

Even full airgapping doesn't guarantee safety. OpenAI researcher Noam Brown recently pointed out that two physically separated computers could theoretically still communicate through temperature sensors, with one heating up its CPU while the other detects the change. Measures like airgapping or monitoring chains of thought buy time, Brown says, but the alignment problem still needs to be solved.

Brown raises harder questions. How will anyone notice when AI starts improving itself (recursive self-improvement, or RSI)? And if the industry builds billions of superintelligent systems that far surpass humans, who ensures they stay aligned? Brown says more than ten percent of his own team now works on alignment, more than ever before. Ad

items.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN
items.summary: CVE-2026-104935 affects Ivanti Connect Secure and it can be exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution with elevated privileges. The post Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Ivanti on Tuesday warned customers that a zero-day vulnerability in its Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances has been exploited in the wild.

Tracked as CVE-2026-104935 and rated high severity, the issue is an authentication bypass that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary commands. Ivanti says it’s aware of exploitation affecting a limited number of customers.

Volexity discovered the in-the-wild exploitation while investigating an incident at one of its customers. A previously undocumented threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 had chained three zero-days to gain unauthenticated, root-level code execution on a fully patched ICS appliance.

According to Volexity, CVE-2026-104935 covers two of the flaws: an authentication bypass and a remote code execution bug. Ivanti has patched these vulnerabilities with the release of ICS versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0, and 25.1.3.1.

The third vulnerability, a privilege escalation issue, remains unpatched, and the vendor plans to fix it over the coming weeks.

Volexity, which found evidence of exploitation starting on October 3, says UTA0576 focused primarily on credential theft, data exfiltration, network reconnaissance, and log tampering. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The attackers stole domain credentials stored on the appliance and exfiltrated limited Active Directory metadata. Using a custom tool, they searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.

They also ran password-spraying attacks, tested credentials with a custom Kerberos tool, and tried to extract credentials from captured network traffic. They also scanned the network, collected the appliance’s configuration data, and parsed authentication logs to identify valid usernames. Volexity found no backdoor or web shell on the device.

The operation was detected and disrupted before the attackers’ ultimate goals became clear. Volexity believes with high confidence that their actions pointed to preparation for lateral movement and a wider compromise of the network.

“Volexity assesses with low confidence that UTA0576 has criminal, rather than espionage, motivations based on the target of this activity,” the company says .

“As with many other threat actor operations Volexity has investigated in 2026, Volexity assesses with medium confidence that UTA0576 makes use of large language models (LLMs) for exploit development and post-exploitation activity,” it added.

When I was eight, I remember our train to Mumbai ground to a halt with a great noise. When we started moving again, a good eight hours later, someone pointed out a mangled tail, of all things, hanging from a branch close to the tracks.

The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs. For a long time, I thought such things only happened in places like rural India, but I learned a few years ago that wildlife and infrastructure do not mix anywhere on the planet.

The FAA estimates that wildlife strikes have cost U.S. civil aviation about $272 million a year on average between 1990 and 2025. In France, the rail operator SNCF says wandering animals affect more than 8,000 trains across the country each year and are among its five leading causes of delays. In Brittany, 120 trains hit animals in 2023 alone, disrupting 660 services and causing more than 15,000 minutes of delays.

Reading about all that damage, to both infrastructure and animals, inspired Sara Nozkova (pictured above on the left) to develop a wildlife-deterrent system that works differently from the sirens, lights, fences, falcons, and culling traditionally used to keep animals away from roads, train tracks, airports, and other infrastructure.

“I was convinced the answer was not a louder deterrent,” she told TechCrunch.

After spending 13 years working in transportation and autonomous vehicles, Nozkova had learned how quickly the systems we build to navigate roads and other controlled environments fail once nature enters the equation.

“We have taught machines to be brilliant, but only inside the environments we engineered for them,” she said. “Cities, factory lines, warehouses. Fixed geometry, known objects. Stepping outside into nature, I saw firsthand how the same machines quickly go blind. Because nature is complex and always alive.”

So instead she joined the AI lab at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm and started working on a system that could change its deterrent responses based on what an animal nearby is doing, and even what kind of animal it is.

That work turned into Flox Intelligence , which spun out of KTH in 2020 and is one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 pitch competition at TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this year at Moscone West in San Francisco October 13-15.

Flox makes edge devices that process data on-site rather than in the cloud. Like autonomous vehicles, they use perception systems to sense their surroundings, but theirs are trained on wildlife behavior. A motion sensor wakes the device when it detects movement, triggering a camera that uses on-device models to identify nearby animals. The device then emits a species-appropriate sound to scare them away.

Nozkova says the system learns from experience, too, and varies its responses so animals don’t get habituated to repeated signals.

The company currently sells battery-operated devices that can be mounted on poles, trees, and other structures. It also offers a software platform that shows clients where the devices are deployed and what’s happening on the ground. The platform can also generate reports for regulatory compliance and for uses like biodiversity monitoring. The longer-term goal is to make the software portable enough to run on machines that work outside, including trains, cars, and drones.

Nozkova says about 150 Flox devices are live in North America, Europe, and Australia at airfields and airport perimeters, road and rail corridors (especially fence ends and crossings along wildlife corridors), national parks, agricultural land, urban areas, mining sites, and critical infrastructure such as electrical substations.

items.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
items.summary: Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic. The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-
items.content:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.

The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."

Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.

"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said . "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."

The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.

A threat actor could build a distributed LLM botnet from poorly secured IoT devices, making it powerful enough to run a capable model. Some of the ways an AI worm could propagate include -

In its test of 11 open-weights models from Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta MoonShot AI, OpenAI, and Zhipu AI (aka Z.ai), Anthropic said it found GLM-5.2 to be the only model to propagate Llama3.1-8B reliably to 8/8 nodes running the redroid Android emulator in 4 out of 5 trials.

It also revealed that an AI IoT worm powered by inexpensive Android TV boxes could be a "slow, distributed" system that can produce a meaningful amount of AI computation when a fleet comprising hundreds of thousands of such devices is networked together to run an inference engine.

Alternatively, it could take the form of a potent cyber model capable of breaching data centers at a high pace, or a model that scams people for compute credits.

"We don't yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves)," Anthropic said.

"We expect AI botnets to infect more than IoT devices, and to use weight-based replication as just one strategy in their playbook. AI botnets could also act intelligently to counter defenders, but we haven’t tested this."

AI agents are already accessing sensitive data and systems—learn how to discover them, control their permissions, and reduce insider risk before it becomes a breach.

UK Housing Ombudsman Service investigates 'security incident'

The U.K. Housing Ombudsman Service is investigating a third-party IT security incident that impacted its case management system on Tuesday.

Established under the Housing Act 1996, the Housing Ombudsman is an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Ministry of Housing, Communities, and Local Government.

The watchdog settles disputes between social housing residents and social landlords in England, including housing associations, landlords, managers, and letting agents.

On Tuesday, the service added an alert to its official website, warning that it's working with the affected service provider to assess the incident's impact and said social housing residents cannot file new complaints until systems are back online.

Those who must raise new complaints are advised to call the Housing Ombudsman's phone line or email the watchdog at info@housing-ombudsman.org.uk.

"The incident has been contained, and we are working with our external supplier to establish the full facts, including the extent of the data involved," the service said . "We are continuing to investigate whether any personal information has been affected and will provide further updates as soon as we are able. "

Housing Ombudsman Service alert (BleepingComputer)

The Housing Ombudsman service has also notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) of the incident and advised tenants and leaseholders to be wary of potential scams when receiving unsolicited messages.

"As a precaution, we recommend that individuals continue to exercise their usual caution when responding to unexpected communications," it added. "Do not disclose personal information unless you are confident of the identity of the requester and report any suspicious activity to the relevant organisation or authorities. "

The watchdog is working to restore its services "as quickly as possible" and will share further updates on the investigation as soon as they're available.

In March, the British government agency Companies House, which operates the registry for all U.K. companies, was also forced to take its WebFiling service offline to fix a security flaw that had exposed companies' information since October 2025.

Two months earlier, in January, the United Kingdom announced a new cybersecurity strategy , backed by more than £210 million ($283 million) and aiming to boost cyber defenses across government departments and the wider public sector.

items.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
items.summary: A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it. The flaw was in the feature that conver
items.content:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.

The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.

The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.

Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.

The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.

Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.

Each personal access token acts as the account that owns it, at a permission level chosen when the token is created. While the flaw was open, conversion changed the owner recorded for each token and left its secret unchanged.

An attacker could abuse this by creating a token on an account they controlled, converting that account into an organization, and naming another user as its owner. The token would then work at the registry as that user.

The named owner was not asked to confirm the change and was not notified, according to Docker and the researchers who reported the flaw. Docker's conversion page has included the sentence "The new owner receives a notification email" since at least August 2024.

Within the token's permission level, a transferred token could pull, push, or delete images in the named owner's repositories and in organizations the owner could access.

Docker rated the flaw critical because that access "includes publishing images under a legitimate name," it said.

In March and April, attackers used stolen publisher credentials to push malicious Trivy images and malicious KICS images to the publishers' own Docker Hub repositories, according to Docker.

Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com found the flaw and reported it to Docker, which says it deployed the fix less than four hours after receiving their report. They named the flaw GhostPat.

In their technical write-up , the two say they reproduced the flaw twice on consenting test accounts. They logged in to the registry as the target account, created and pushed to a repository in its namespace, pushed to an organization it belonged to, and pulled its private repositories.

Docker reviewed every account conversion made while the flaw was open and compared them with registry logs and token records. It looked for any token used under more than one identity and examined every push made with a transferred token, about 304,000 in all.

"We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited," the company said.

Every one of those pushes went to a repository belonging to the converted organization or to its named owner, according to Docker. In the large majority of cases, both accounts belonged to the same person or team.

Where it could not confirm that one person controlled both accounts, Docker analyzed the highest-risk public images without running them and found no malware or tampering.

Docker's registry logs show when a token is used, not that it exists, so a transferred token that was never used left no record in the logs. For that reason, Docker treated every token transferred by a conversion while the flaw was open as possibly affected, whether or…

items.content:
Gemini 4 Argon is now available worldwide as Google's most capable frontier model

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally, making its new flagship AI model available to developers, businesses, and consumers starting today.

Gemini 4 Argon is accessible through the API in AI Studio and the Gemini platform , according to Google. Google AI Ultra subscribers can use the model in Google Antigravity , while AI Ultra and Pro subscribers get access through the Gemini app and Google Search's AI mode .

Not everyone benefits equally, though. Free Gemini users and paying Plus subscribers now only have access to the weaker Flash models under a new model tier structure . Argon replaces the Gemini Pro class as Google's new frontier series. Google says more Gemini 4 models will follow, which likely means updated Flash variants that would eventually trickle down to free and Plus users as well. Internally, Google is reportedly already testing a potential successor codenamed " Carbon ," which is supposed to outperform Argon at coding in particular. Ad

Pricing and benchmark results remain as previously reported : $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens at the introductory rate, with a 95 percent discount on cached inputs. Argon holds the top spot on the Vals Index, but it still trails Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 in independent overall rankings. And because Google waited roughly two weeks to ship, it now also sits behind Meta's Muse Wonder Full , which launched just yesterday. Ad

*Google doesn't state this figure explicitly but says the cache is 95 percent cheaper than the regular input token price.

Google's benchmark results. | Image: Google

Google says Argon turned months of internal engineering into weeks

Google shared some internal numbers with the launch, though they're self-reported. Software engineers using Argon increased agent-driven code submissions by more than 35 percent, while code rollbacks dropped by nearly a third, the company says. Ad

In the Chromium project, Argon helped the Chrome team complete an architectural refactor across hundreds of files within the 40-million-line codebase. Work that would have taken months was finished in a few weeks. For users, the payoff is that web pages can move between tabs, sidebars, and floating windows without needing to reload.

Working with Google's open-source Agent Development Kit , Argon ran autonomously overnight and found optimizations that cut session preparation time by 40 percent and sped up cold imports by 21 percent. Inference speed for the open Gemma models on an A100 via vLLM jumped by a factor of 2.85, from roughly 37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second. The changes are visible in upstream pull requests . Ad

Argon can also generate complex 3D models, games, and animations in pure code that run directly in the browser. One demo features a raytracing engine written entirely in Python with no external libraries. Google published the source code . Ad

In the demo below, Argon starts from a single image in Antigravity and controls Blender via MCP in an autonomous loop. It modeled gothic architecture and set up audio-reactive lighting to produce a finished 3D scene, Google says.

3D remains a weak spot for Meta's Muse models, which according to Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang were not specifically trained for 3D demo games.

Google offers 10,000 researchers free access and claims its strongest safety record yet

Google is also offering 10,000 researchers the highest usage tier of Google Antigravity free for six months. Spots are awarded on a rolling basis depending on eligibility, capacity, and selection. Applications are open now.
