앤트로픽이 이미 서비스 중인 플래그십 모델 환경을 활용해 차세대 체크포인트의 실전 라우팅(Routing) 테스트에 착수한 정황이 포착됐다. 정식 출시나 발표가 이뤄지지 않은 상태에서 기존 모델 트래픽의 일부를 미공개 고성능 모델로 우회시키는 '셰도우 디플로이먼트(Shadow Deployment)' 및 'A/B 테스트(A/B Testing)'가 진행되면서, 개발자와 테스터들 사이에서 폭발적인 반응과 함께 성능 분석이 이어지고 있다.

12일(현지시간) 테스팅카탈로그 등에 따르면, 이번 차세대 모델 테스트는 앤트로픽이 최상위 모델인 '오퍼스 5.5'를 시장에 선보인 지 불과 3주 만에 수면 위로 떠올랐다.

X와 기술 커뮤니티 테스터들은 평소와 동일한 오퍼스 5.5 환경에 접속해 대화를 나누던 중 출력물의 품질이 이전과 비교할 수 없을 정도로 급상승한 현상을 감지했다.

테스터들은 이러한 백엔드 우회 테스트를 간파하는 구체적인 요령과 단서들을 공유하고 있다. 대표적으로 오퍼스 5.5 모델에게 "VoxelBench를 아는가. 검색은 사용하지 말고 답하라"와 같은 질문을 던졌을 때, 기존 모델이 인지하지 못하는 미공개 데이터나 개념에 대해 막힘없이 답변해 내는 현상이 지목됐다.

이는 모델의 지능 향상뿐만 아니라 백엔드에 새롭게 투입된 학습 데이터 체계와 체크포인트가 기존 채널에 섞여 들어왔음을 시사한다. 커뮤니티에서는 이번에 테스트 중인 모델의 가칭으로 '클로드 넥스트(Claude Next)' '오퍼스 5.6' 또는 '페이블 5.5' 등을 거론하며 촉각을 곤두세우고 있다.

실제로 잠복 테스트 채널을 통해 노출된 차세대 모델의 출력 결과물은 기존 모델의 한계를 뛰어넘는 성능을 보여준다는 평이다. X 사용자 마마덕(marmaduke091)은 블렌더(Blender)의 MCP를 활용하도록 단 한 줄의 프롬프트만 입력한 상태에서, 모델이 외부 에셋을 전혀 쓰지 않고 바닥부터 복잡한 삼차원 장정에 이르는 고난도 작업을 스스로 완벽하게 완성해 내는 시연 영상을 공개했다. 테스터들은 이를 지금까지 어떤 모델에서도 보지 못한 가장 뛰어난 결과물로 평가했다.

This is with just a simple one sentence prompt. It worked for 2 hours with Blender MCP to create it from scratch, no ready made model was used.

This is the single most impressive output I've got from a model so far. pic.twitter.com/qIKUjYJbiB

또 다른 테스터인 체타슬루아(Chetaslua)는 차세대 모델이 자바스크립트(JS) 코딩만으로 '인간의 삶'을 주제로 한 애니메이션의 모든 프레임을 직접 그려내는 과정을 공유했다. 단 두 개의 짧은 프롬프트와 약 2시간의 작업 시간, 2700만 토큰에 달하는 집중적인 연산 노력이 투입된 이 결과물은 기존 오퍼스 5.5조차 뒤처지게 보이게 만들 만큼 엄청난 수준의 디테일을 과시했다는 평을 받고 있다.

Claude Next is being tested on claude code

and i thought it will take a month to make image and video gen model obsolete i was wrong

Behold the supremacy , fully coded ,this akes even Opus 5.5 look primitive

I will upload more test different types its SOTA in every f#ing… https://t.co/AS5C5WXj6z pic.twitter.com/6v22g50dph

— Chetaslua (@chetaslua) October 11, 2026

이 외에도 음악 생성 모델 수노나 보컬 생성 도구인 엘레븐랩스, 쓰리제이에스(Three.js) 등을 연동해 모델 자신의 소개를 담은 종교 뮤지컬 '호산나(Hosanna)'를 구축하는 등 멀티모달과 멀티미디어 영역에서 다양한 실험 결과가 잇달아 등장하고 있다. 일각에서는 이러한 추세라면 이미지 및 비디오 생성 모델의 효용성마저 위협받을 수 있다는 관측이 나온다.

Me and @chetaslua just asked Fable 5.5 to create a song introducing itself, and it made a full-blown religious musical called “Hosanna,” with the model singing its own introduction.

It used my Suno for the music, ElevenLabs for the vocals, and built a synchronized Three.js… pic.twitter.com/69FKrEWsqW

이처럼 소셜미디어에서 차세대 모델의 성능 찬사가 이어지자, 앤트로픽의 파트너십 및 홍보 담당 매니저인 존 호프먼은 관련 게시물에 "최고의 순간은 아직 오지 않았다. 계속 지켜봐 달라"는 댓글을 남겨 기대감을 고조시켰다.

The best is yet to come. Stay tuned peeps https://t.co/xE0oAFFjIi

— John Hoffmann (@johnjhoffmann) October 11, 2026

이처럼 정식 출시 전에 기존 서비스 채널을 통해 신규 모델을 테스트하는 방식은 앤트로픽만의 전유물이 아니다. 사내 벤치마크나 통제된 환경에서의 소규모 검증만으로는 전 세계 수백만명의 사용자가 던지는 예측 불가능한 대규모 트래픽과 복잡한 프롬프트 부하를 완벽히 감당할 수 없기 때문이다.

이 때문에 오픈AI나 구글 등도 대규모 업데이트 직전에는 기존 서비스 모델의 트래픽 일부를 미공개 체크포인트로 조용히 라우팅해 실무 안정성과 성능을 최종 점검하는 방식을 관례적으로 활용해 온 것으로 알려졌다. 실제로 구글은 최근 안티그래비티 플랫폼의 A/B 테스트를 통해 '제미나이 4 아르곤'을 노출한 것으로 알려졌다.

앤트로픽도 오퍼스 5.5 제품군으로 가격 경쟁력을 다진 데 이어, 초고성능 티어의 차세대 모델을 실전 환경에서 검증하며 차세대 모델 경쟁에 대비한다는 분석이다.

items.content:
AI 스타트업 타입세이프가 공개한 의사결정 모델 '제브(Jev)'를 둘러싸고 표절 논란이 불거졌다. 콘브이 이노베이션스(ConvAI Innovations)의 설립자 난다키쇼르 무쿤노스는 제브의 핵심 아키텍처가 자신의 기존 연구와 유사하다며, 관련 아이디어와 기술을 먼저 개발했다고 주장했다.

톰스하드웨어에 따르면, 무쿤노스는 지닌달 타입세이프가 제브를 공개한 직후 블로그를 통해 "1년 전에 이미 제브 아키텍처를 설계했다"고 밝혔다.

그는 2025년 3월30일 공개한 ' 세일즈RL에이전트(SalesRLAgent) ' 논문과 함께 모델 가중치, 데이터셋을 공개했으며, 같은 해 9월 발표한 후속 논문도 제브의 작동 방식과 밀접하게 일치한다고 주장했다.

자신의 연구가 특정 산업 분야의 문제를 해결하는 데 초점을 맞췄기 때문에 충분한 주목을 받지 못했다고 토로했다. 반면 타이프세이프는 비슷한 개념을 범용 의사결정 엔진으로 발전시켜 상용 제품으로 선보였다는 설명이다. 다만 현재 제기된 주장은 무쿤노스 측의 입장이며, 표절 여부가 독립적으로 입증된 것은 아니다.

제브는 기존 대형언어모델(LLM)과 달리 긴 텍스트를 생성하는 대신, 입력 데이터와 질문을 바탕으로 특정 선택지의 확률을 계산하는 의사결정 모델이다. 고객의 구매 내역을 입력하면 반품 의사가 있는지, 어떤 상품을 지칭하는지 등을 확률값으로 출력한다. 개발자는 이 결과를 프로그램의 조건문에 연결해 자동화된 의사결정에 활용할 수 있다.

이 방식은 답변을 토큰 단위로 생성하거나 긴 대화 기록을 유지할 필요가 없어 기존 LLM보다 빠르고 비용이 적게 들 수 있다. 답변을 확률 형태로 직접 제공하기 때문에 자연어 생성 과정에서 발생하는 일부 환각 문제도 줄일 수 있다는 장점이 있다.

제브가 공개된 뒤에는 마이크로소프트의 '디시전(Decision)', 오픈AI의 '디시전스 API(Decisions API)', 패스티노의 '글라이드(Glide)' 등 유사한 서비스가 잇따라 등장했다. 클라우드플레어의 '클레프(Clef)'와 퍼플렉시티의 '디사이더(Decider)'를 비롯해 다양한 오픈소스 프로젝트도 등장하면서 경쟁이 빠르게 확대되고 있다.

이들 모델 상당수는 기존 경량 모델에 입력과 출력, 의사결정 과정을 제어하는 구조를 추가하는 방식으로 개발됐다. 알리바바의 오픈소스 모델 '큐원(Qwen)' 계열을 활용하는 사례가 많은 것으로 알려졌다.

무쿤노스는 논란에 대응해 오픈소스 모델 '라야(Laya)'도 공개했다. 라야는 제브와 유사한 방식으로 작동하며, 사용자가 자체 하드웨어에서 실행할 수 있도록 설계됐다. 다국어도 지원한다. 제브 계열 모델이 주로 큐원 같은 LLM 기반 모델을 활용하는 것과 달리, 라야는 버트(BERT) 계열의 인코더 전용 모델을 기반으로 한다.

Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released

Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB5127648 and KB5126653 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs, and add new features.

Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the October 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.

You can install today's update by going to  Start  >  Settings  >  Windows Update  and clicking on  'Check for Updates .'

You can also manually download and install the update from the  Microsoft Update Catalog .

This is the tenth 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.

What's new in the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update

With today's update, Microsoft is adding new emojis to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.

Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:

New! This update adjusts how the preview pane handles files downloaded from the web. For HTML files, a new Preview anyway button lets you acknowledge the warning and preview the file. Non-HTML files, such as PDFs, are now previewed automatically.

New! File Explorer Home now preserves the state of sections (expanded or collapsed), so you can pick up where you left off.

New! This update improves the reliability of thumbnail previews for cloud files in the Details pane. The pane has also been reorganized so file properties are easier to find and review at a glance.

New! The update addresses an issue that could clear the address bar contents when entering edit mode by clicking near the right side of the address bar.

New! This update adds support for Emoji 17.0 , including new emoji such as distorted face, fight cloud, and hairy creature. To insert them, press Windows + . to open the emoji panel.

New! This update also refines the design of several existing emoji for better consistency across platforms, including saluting face, face with peeking eye, goose, lotus, and kissing cat.

[Widgets] New! This update introduces the Tips widget, which provides short, helpful guidance about Windows features. To add it to your Widgets board, open the board, select Add widgets , and then choose Tips . To add it to your lock screen, go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen and add Tips to your lock screen widgets.

[Personalization] This update includes a variety of improvements to desktop background experiences.

This update improves the reliability of the Personalization > Background page in Settings .

This update adds support for using DIB image files as desktop backgrounds.

This update improves reliability of desktop slideshow transitions on newly created accounts.

This update improves resolution of previews when selecting a desktop background in Personalization > Background .

This update improves desktop background preview display in Settings for users with portrait mode monitors.

This update improves reliability of processing desktop wallpaper changes when they happen in quick succession.

This update adds support for using slideshow wallpapers with multiple desktops, so that it won’t automatically switch you back to Picture.

This update contains several enhancements to improve reliability and experience when connecting to and using Bluetooth devices:

During voice calls, the Windows shell volume flyout now appears when adjusting the volume of a Bluetooth Classic Audio accessory via the volume controls on the accessory, providing visual feedback of the new volume level.

This update improves the accuracy of the connection state displayed by Windows for accessories that have disconnected from the PC.

This update improves stability of the Bluetooth and devices page in Settings when managing Bluetooth and audio devices.

오픈AI가 '코덱스'와 '챗GPT 워크'에서 사용하는 'GPT-6.1 솔'의 기본 컨텍스트 길이를 기존 27만2000 토큰에서 50만 토큰으로 확대했다. 약 80% 늘어난 규모로, 장시간 작업에서 발생하는 맥락 압축을 줄이고 복잡한 작업의 세부 사항을 더 오래 유지하도록 지원하기 위한 조치다.

티보 소티오 오픈AI 제품 담당 책임자는 12일(현지시간) 이 같은 변경 사항을 공개했다. 이는 오픈AI가 진행 중인 28일 연속 코덱스 성능 개선 이벤트의 7일 차 업데이트 내역이다.

컨텍스트 길이는 AI 모델이 한 번에 참고하고 처리할 수 있는 정보의 양을 뜻한다. 길이가 늘어나면 대규모 코드베이스나 긴 대화, 여러 단계로 이어지는 작업에서 앞선 정보와 세부 조건을 더 많이 유지할 수 있다.

이번 조정의 핵심은 컨텍스트 압축(compaction) 발생 빈도를 줄이는 데 있다. 모델이 처리할 정보가 컨텍스트 한도를 넘어서면 기존 내용을 요약해 공간을 확보해야 하는데, 이 과정에서 중요한 세부 사항이나 미묘한 맥락이 누락될 수 있다. 기본 컨텍스트 길이가 늘어나면 모델이 정보를 압축해야 하는 상황이 줄어들어 장시간 작업의 연속성과 정확성을 높이는 데 도움이 된다.

We have increased default context length for GPT-6.1 Sol to 500k when used through Codex & Work, up from 272k or an ~ 80% increase.

We will go higher in the future, but it helps reduce occurrence of compactions and with tasks that require keeping a lot of context and…

소티오는 새 기본값이 충분한 테스트를 거쳐 대부분 사용자에게 적합한 수준으로 설정됐다고 설명했다. 그는 “대부분 사용자에게 가장 적합한 지점”이라는 취지로 50만 토큰 설정의 의미를 강조하면서, 앞으로 기본 컨텍스트 길이를 더 확대할 계획이라고 밝혔다.

사용자가 직접 설정을 조정할 수 있다는 점도 유지된다. 50만 토큰보다 더 큰 컨텍스트가 필요한 경우 값을 높일 수 있고, 반대로 자원 사용을 줄이려면 낮출 수도 있다. GPT-6.1 솔이 지원하는 최대 컨텍스트 길이는 100만 토큰이다.

이번 업데이트는 특히 대규모 프로젝트를 다루는 개발자와 장시간 코딩 작업을 수행하는 사용자에게 유용할 것으로 보인다. 여러 파일과 코드 변경 이력, 복잡한 요구사항을 동시에 참고해야 하는 작업에서 맥락을 반복적으로 요약하거나 정보를 다시 입력해야 하는 부담을 줄일 수 있기 때문이다.

items.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
items.summary: An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately."
items.content:
An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity.

Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti, found the attack on one customer's appliance. The appliance was fully patched at the time and running version 22.8R2.4. The attacker, which Volexity tracks as UTA0576, began exploiting it on October 3.

Ivanti said on October 13 that it is aware of "limited exploitation in the wild."

The first two flaws are an authentication bypass and a remote code execution flaw, tracked together as CVE-2026-104935 . Together they let an attacker run code as the appliance's cgi-server user, and the third flaw, a privilege escalation, raises that to root, Volexity said.

The CVE record Ivanti filed shows which Connect Secure versions are affected:

Ivanti's security advisory has more on the affected versions and the fixes.

The release notes for 25.1.3.0 are dated July 2026. Customers already on that version are outside the range the CVE record gives.

Ivanti is working on a fix for the privilege escalation flaw, which will come "in a future release in the coming weeks," Volexity said. Its report does not say what risk that flaw carries on an appliance where the first two are fixed.

Ivanti tells customers to upgrade and to run its Integrity Checker Tool regularly. That tool misses this chain, Volexity said, because the exploit changes library code only in memory and restores the configuration data it alters. The attacker also took steps to stay hidden from the tool.

Confirming a compromise takes forensic investigation, including network and memory forensics, according to Volexity. These signs come from the one incident it investigated:

In that incident, the attacker stole stored credentials, including LDAP domain credentials, searched Active Directory for passwords, and ran password-spraying attacks against its accounts. No backdoor or web shell was left behind. The attacker reran the entire exploit chain for each command.

Volexity's report and Ivanti's post do not name a temporary workaround for customers who cannot upgrade yet. They also do not say whether upgrading removes access an attacker has already gained.

Volexity assessed with low confidence that UTA0576's motive is criminal, not espionage. Neither company said how many customers were attacked.

Ivanti rates CVE-2026-104935 8.6 out of 10 on the CVSS severity scale. In its own entry in the CVE record, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) marks exploitation as "active" and the technical impact as "total."

Separately, the same Ivanti post covers fixes for two other products, Xtraction and Neurons Patch for Intune, and Ivanti said it is not aware of those flaws being exploited. Each has a flaw Ivanti rates 9.9 out of 10: CVE-2026-106042 in Xtraction before version 2026.4, and CVE-2026-109412 in Neurons Patch for Intune.

items.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
items.content:

If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.

“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence , told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”

Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.

“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.

Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon , October 13.

Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. In 2023, he and Liu — his then-PhD adviser — published a paper on the subject that made it onto the cover of the top scientific journal Nature. That’s when the calls started coming in from autonomous vehicle companies interested in implementing their ideas.

“I realized that I wanted to build this and take it from purely academic research into a product that’s useful in the real world,” Sun said.

Using their academic research as a base, Sun and Liu built Laplace, so named for “Laplace’s demon,” an 1814 thought experiment by French scholar Pierre-Simon Laplace, who imagined that if you knew the exact state of everything in the universe, you could predict the future with total precision.

“We are essentially using simulation to predict the real world’s future,” Sun said.

At the startup’s core is a high-fidelity simulation reconstructed from the real world, paired with an AI agent that constantly probes for weaknesses and failure points. The goal is to ensure that any physical AI — be it a robot, autonomous vehicle, or smart city solution — is safe in simulation before it’s deployed in the real world.

The simulation environment is a post-trained version of Nvidia’s Cosmos, an AI world simulation platform, which is grounded in the real world, allowing Laplace to reconstruct anything from an Arizona highway to a Paris pedestrian crossing. Simulations are generated by blending a mesh of different real-world information. A Google Street View image could serve as a reference from which an entire street is generated. But rather than generating something random, the simulator combines real-world map data to re-create an environment that’s true to scale.

Developers can then use language prompts to change the setting in real time, like adding in afternoon traffic. Sun says Laplace pulls real-time traffic and congestion information from navigation providers like TomTom.

Within Laplace’s simulations, not only is the environment simulated, but also the behavior of other actors. For example, during a demo, Sun directed the test agent vehicle to swerve into oncoming traffic. The car it would have hit — or driven through, as is common among some generative world models — moved out of its way to avoid a collision.

“It’s truly an interactive simulation environment,” Sun said. “Everyone is reacting to everything … This is more like a world model with interactive participants.”

items.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
items.summary: A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's o
items.content:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2 , released on August 21, as the fix.

The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.

Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.

Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.

Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.

The Hacker News ran SAP's own tests for the check on October 13, against the source code of every release from 0.45.1 to 0.58.4 and of the three 0.36 releases. The six releases failed 9 of the 11 tests SAP added with version 0.55.1. That version and the 11 releases after it passed all 11.

As of October 13, the advisory lists no version above 0.45.2 as affected. Neither it nor the release notes say whether the six releases fall under CVE-2026-89111.

Two releases on the older 0.36 line also lack the check. Versions 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 were published on September 4 and September 10, after the August fix, and failed the tests SAP wrote for it. Both fall inside the advisory's range of versions below 0.45.2.

Versions 0.45.2 through 0.52.2 and 0.55.1 through 0.58.4 contain the check. Version 0.58.4 was the newest release on PyPI, the Python package index, on October 13.

Upgrading within the 0.36 line does not add the check. None of its three releases contains it.

Applications that cannot upgrade yet can compare each tenant subdomain with a list of their registered tenants before passing it to the SDK, SAP says in the advisory.

The flaw matters only where an application passes a tenant subdomain to the SDK. The August fix covered three modules: Agent Gateway, Destination and Document Management Service.

The advisory does not say whether applications that ran a release without the check should replace their client credentials.

When an application passes a tenant subdomain, the SDK requests an access token for that tenant. To do that, it takes the token URL from the application's configuration and replaces part of it with the tenant subdomain.

Releases without the check used whatever value they were given. The SDK then sent the application's client ID and client secret to the resulting URL to request the token.

An attacker who controls the tenant subdomain can point that request at their own server, according to SAP.

The check accepts only a single name made of letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters long. Any other value stops the request with an error.

SAP labels the flaw server-side request forgery (SSRF), a weakness in which a server can be made to send a request to a destination it did not intend.

What an attacker could do with the credentials depends on what the application's client is allowed to do. The advisory does not say.

The unchecked code was in the SDK from its first release on PyPI, on March 16.

The August release notes list the fix under "Bug Fixes" and do not mention security.…

items.content:
AI의 영상 제작 기술이 발전하면서 원하는 장면과 움직임을 얼마나 정확하게 구현하느냐가 핵심 과제로 떠오르고 있다. 마이크로소프트(MS)는 코드로 영상의 구조와 동작을 설계해 생성 과정을 직접 제어하는 새로운 접근법을 제시했다.

MS는 11일(현지시간) 실행 가능한 코드를 활용해 영상의 장면 구성과 객체 움직임, 카메라 경로 등을 정밀하게 제어하는 ' 코드 비디오 모델(Code Video Model) '을 공개했다.

기존 비디오 생성 모델이 장면의 물리적 움직임과 객체 배치를 내부적으로 처리하는 방식에서 벗어나, 코드로 장면을 설계하고 움직임을 계산해 영상 생성 과정을 직접 제어하는 것이 특징이다.

이 모델은 프롬프트를 실행 가능한 프로그램으로 변환하는 코딩 에이전트를 비디오 생성 엔진으로 활용한다. 사용자가 원하는 장면을 설명하면 에이전트가 객체의 위치와 움직임, 타이밍, 카메라 이동 경로 등을 코드로 작성한다. 여기에 물리 방정식을 적용해 객체의 동작을 계산하고, 실행 결과로 프록시 비디오와 참조 이미지를 생성한다.

프록시 비디오는 최종 영상을 만들기 전에 장면의 구조와 움직임을 확인하는 일종의 '미리보기 영상'이다. 이를 만드는 데 걸리는 시간은 1분 이내다.

이후 사전 학습된 비디오 생성(R2V·Reference-to-Video) 모델이 프록시 비디오의 구조와 참조 이미지의 외관을 바탕으로 디테일한 최종 영상을 생성한다.

코딩 에이전트가 사용자의 요청을 실행 가능한 프로그램과 미리보기 영상(프록시 비디오)으로 변환해 장면 구성과 움직임을 제어한다. 이어 대표 프레임의 스타일을 조정해 만든 참고 이미지와 미리보기 영상 정보를 초기 단계에 반영하고, R2V 모델을 통해 최종 영상을 생성한다. (사진=MS)

연구진은 이 방식이 영상 생성의 제어 가능성을 높인다고 설명했다. 기존 비디오 확산 모델은 현실적인 영상을 만들 수 있지만, 객체의 배치나 움직임, 카메라 궤적이 내부적으로 결정돼 사용자가 세부 요소를 직접 조정하기 어렵다. 반면 코드 비디오 모델은 장면의 구성 요소가 코드로 표현되기 때문에 특정 객체의 움직임이나 카메라 경로 등을 수정할 수 있다.

다만 프록시 비디오를 그대로 최종 생성 과정에 반영하면 영상이 평면적이고 단순한 모습으로 나타날 수 있다. 연구진은 이를 해결하기 위해 별도의 학습 없이 적용할 수 있는 '초기 단계 조건화(early-step conditioning)' 기술을 도입했다.

이 기술은 영상 생성 초기 샘플링 단계에서만 프록시 비디오를 참고하도록 하고, 이후 단계에서는 해당 조건을 제거한다. 초기에는 프록시 비디오를 통해 장면의 구조와 움직임을 유지하고, 후반에는 참조 이미지의 외관과 시각적 품질을 살리는 방식이다. 이를 통해 구조적 제어와 자연스러운 영상 표현을 동시에 확보하도록 설계했다.

연구진은 다양한 활용 사례를 평가하기 위해 게임, 장면 편집, 물리 기반 움직임, 불릿 타임 효과, 3D·4D 재구성 등을 포함한 벤치마크 '코드비디오벤치(CodeVideoBench)'도 제시했다.

R2V 모델 '미니맥스-H3(MiniMax-H3)'를 결합한 코드 비디오 모델은 평가에 사용된 큐원VL-3.8-27B, GPT-5.6, GPT-6 기준으로 각각 85.2점, 82.1점, 85.8점을 기록했다. 기존 학습 기반 모델 가운데 가장 높은 성능을 보인 VACE의 점수는 같은 기준에서 각각 74.3점, 73.1점, 80.6점이었다.

연구진은 코드 기반 영상 생성이 물리적으로 일관된 움직임 구현뿐 아니라 3D·4D 재구성, 로봇 시뮬레이션, 월드 모델 학습 데이터 생성 등으로 확장될 수 있다고 설명했다.

코드 비디오 모델의 가중치와 관련 코드는 허깅페이스 와 깃허브 를 통해 제공된다.

items.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
items.summary: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.
items.content:
Disrupt 2026 has officially begun. Grab your pass now to be at the center of the startup epicenter. REGISTER NOW

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

Illustrating the pace of AI tool adoption within enterprises driving such fears, Shahar Bahat, CEO and co-founder of Pluto Security , says a newly announced AI tool can show up inside companies’ environment within a mere two hours of its release. And about 60% of the risks her company detects across its customer base are in tools vibe-coded by non-developers: Finance departments are the biggest source of such risks, she told TechCrunch, followed by marketing and legal teams. Developers rank fourth, she said.

Her startup’s tools apparently found a vibe-coded app made by a finance employee at a Fortune 500 company to manage customer information and churn, but the app was left exposed to the internet.

Pluto, fresh out of stealth with $42 million in funding, is the latest in a new crop of security startups that have quickly sprung up to help companies address those fears gaps, and all of them are raising big money from investors on the back of the conviction that only using existing security software to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, and usage is a square-peg-round-hole approach.

Bahat tells TechCrunch her startup started selling only in April and has already found some takers for its tech, which helps companies gain context, risk analysis, visibility, and control over how their employees use AI tools. She said Pluto began selling in April and has already crossed $2 million in annual recurring revenue, with more than 30 enterprise customers, including Oscar Health, Workato, Sixt, and AlphaSense.

Pluto’s funding spans an $8.5 million seed round led by TLV Partners, with cybersecurity firm Armis’ founders also investing. The company recently raised a Series A of $34 million led by Jump Capital, with Skinos (Check Point co-founder Shlomo Kramer’s venture firm), Ansa Capital, and other angel investors participating.

That’s decent traction for a young startup, though not unique in this AI era. But it may be because the breadth of the risk isn’t isolated to large tech companies that lead the AI adoption charts.

items.content:
멀티모달 AI 에이전트 도입이 가속화되는 가운데, 텍스트와 구조화된 데이터 처리에 국한됐던 기존 '의사결정' 모델이 이미지와 오디오, 비디오 등 다양한 입력 정보를 직접 이해하고 판단하는 멀티모달 모델로 빠르게 진화하고 있다.

vLLM 시맨틱 라우터(vLLM Semantic Router) 개발팀은 11일(현지시간) 텍스트와 JSON뿐만 아니라 이미지까지 직접 분석할 수 있는 멀티모달 의사결정 모델 제품군 ‘디시전 3.0(Decision 3.0)’을 오픈소스로 공개했다.

기존 의사결정 모델이 주로 텍스트와 구조화된 데이터에 의존했던 것과 달리, 디시전 3.0은 이미지 속 정보를 직접 처리해 AI 에이전트의 판단과 요청 분류, 안전성 검증을 간소화한 것이 특징이다.

0.8B부터 27B까지 총 5개 크기로 구성됐다. 가장 작은 ‘d3-라이트(lite)’부터 ‘d3-나노(nano)’, ‘d3-미니(mini)’, ‘d3-플래시(flash)’, 대형 모델 ‘d3’까지 제공하며, 모두 허깅페이스 를 통해 아파치 2.0(Apache-2.0) 라이선스로 공개됐다.

의사결정 모델은 질문에 대한 긴 문장을 생성하는 대신 미리 정해진 선택지별 확률을 반환하는 방식으로 작동한다. 개발자가 입력 데이터와 함께 예·아니요 질문이나 객관식 질문, 점수 평가 항목 등을 전달하면 모델은 각 선택지에 대한 확률값을 출력한다. 개발자는 이를 별도의 텍스트 분석 과정 없이 프로그램의 조건문이나 라우팅 규칙에 연결할 수 있다.

기존 시스템에서는 이미지가 포함된 사용자 인터페이스(UI) 화면이나 인포그래픽, 스캔 문서를 분석하려면 먼저 별도의 비전 모델로 이미지에서 텍스트를 추출하는 과정이 필요했다. 디시전 3.0은 모든 모델에 비전 인코더를 내장해 이 같은 중간 단계를 줄였다. PNG, JPEG, WebP 형식의 이미지를 최대 160만 픽셀 해상도로 처리할 수 있으며, 하나의 요청에 여러 이미지를 포함할 수도 있다.

모든 질문에 대한 판단 결과는 확률값으로 제공된다. 다만 각 질문은 입력을 대상으로 개별 순방향 연산을 수행하므로, 질문 수에 따라 연산량이 늘어날 수 있다. 그럼에도 자연어 답변을 생성하고 이를 다시 분석하는 방식보다 파이프라인을 단순화할 수 있어 AI 에이전트의 지연 시간과 운영 비용을 줄이는 데 도움이 될 것으로 기대된다.

디시전 3.0은 알리바바의 '큐원(Qwen)' 계열 모델을 기반으로 미세조정됐다. 가장 큰 d3 모델은 약 260억개의 매개변수를 갖췄으며, 나머지 4개 모델은 약 8억~84억개의 매개변수로 구성됐다.

자체 평가 결과에 따르면, d3 모델은 텍스트 평가에서 64.1점, 비전 평가에서 71.6점을 기록해 퍼플렉시티의 ‘디사이더(Decider) v1.1’보다 높은 점수를 얻었다. 모델 크기를 줄이면서도 약 90억개 매개변수의 d3-플래시가 텍스트 평가에서 이전 세대의 270억개 매개변수급 모델을 앞서는 등 효율성을 입증했다.

디시전 3.0은 AI 에이전트의 요청 분류와 모델 선택, 이미지 기반 UI 분석, 콘텐츠 안전성 검증 등 다양한 분야에 활용할 수 있다. 특히 이미지와 텍스트가 결합된 입력을 처리해야 하는 서비스에서 별도 모델을 연결하는 복잡성을 줄일 수 있다.

클라우드플레어(Cloudflare) 역시 텍스트, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오를 한 번에 처리하는 멀티모달 의사결정 모델 ‘클레프-옴니(Clef-omni)’를 선보이며 트렌드에 합류했다.

9일 공개된 이 모델은 총 300억개 매개변수 중 실제 추론에 활용되는 매개변수가 30억개인 전문가 혼합(MoE) 구조를 채택했다. 허깅페이스 를 통해 오픈 가중치를 제공해 개발자가 자체 환경에서도 실행할 수 있도록 했다.

클레프-옴니는 입력 데이터에서 텍스트를 추출하거나 음성을 전사하고 동영상에 자막을 생성하는 별도 과정을 거치지 않고, 여러 형태의 데이터를 한 번에 분석해 의사결정 결과를 확률값으로 반환한다. 클라우드플레어의 워커스 AI(Workers AI) 환경에서는 이미지 최대 4개, 오디오 클립 최대 4개, 동영상 최대 2개를 한 요청에 포함할 수 있다. 질문은 요청당 최대 64개까지 처리한다.

중앙값 기준 처리 시간은 텍스트 약 130밀리초(ms), 이미지 약 150ms다. 음성이 포함된 21초 분량의 동영상도 약 1.5초 만에 분석할 수 있다. 의도 분류 평가에서는 '뱅킹77(BANKING77)'에서 94.8점, 'CLINC150+OOS'에서 97.7점의 매크로 F1 점수를 기록했다.

다만 모든 평가에서 우위를 보인 것은 아니다. 복잡한 추론과 워크플로 평가에서는 기존 클레프보다 낮은 성능을 기록했으며, 'GPQA 다이아몬드' 평가 점수도 47.4점으로 제브의 78.3점에 미치지 못했다.

이는 다양한 입력 형식을 한 번에 처리하는 능력과 복잡한 추론 성능이 반드시 비례하지는 않는다는 점을 보여준다.

items.content:
AI가 농작물의 수확량을 높이는 핵심 유전자 변이를 찾아내는 데 성공했다. 식물 DNA에 특화된 AI 모델과 범용 언어모델을 결합해 수천개의 후보 변이 가운데 실제 형질 변화와 관련된 변이를 수분 만에 식별한 것이다. 가뭄에 강하거나 더 많은 열매를 맺는 작물을 개발하는 데 AI를 활용할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다.

AI 연구소 리빙 모델스(Living Models)는 6일(현지시간) 식물 DNA를 학습한 모델 ‘보타닉-1(BOTANIC-1)’과 구글의 ‘젬마 4(Gemma 4)’를 결합해 유전자 변이를 분석하는 시스템을 공개했다.

특히 보타닉-1은 어텐션 메커니즘 대신 양방향 Mamba-2(BiMamba2) 구조를 채택해 위치 임베디드 없이도 긴 콘텍스트를 효율적으로 처리하는 것이 특징이다.

젬마 4가 유전자 데이터를 정리하고 분석 과정을 자동화하면, 보타닉-1이 식물의 진화 과정에서 축적된 유전적 특성을 바탕으로 형질에 영향을 줄 가능성이 큰 변이를 평가하는 방식이다.

연구진은 멜론의 수확량과 관련된 유전자 변이를 대상으로 성능을 시험했다. 기존 유전학 분석으로 후보군을 좁혔지만, 염색체상에서 서로 가까이 있는 변이들이 함께 유전되는 특성 때문에 실제 형질 변화를 일으킨 변이를 구분하기는 어려웠다.

일반적인 분석 도구를 활용한 젬마 4는 후보 변이들을 두 개까지 줄였지만, 실제 원인 변이와 관련 없는 변이를 구분하지 못했다. 반면 보타닉-1을 추가하자 분석 결과가 달라졌다. 연구진은 삽입·결실 등 다른 유형의 변이를 걸러낸 뒤 남은 단일염기 변이 2494개를 분석했고, 목표 변이를 4분 이내에 정확히 1위로 찾아냈다.

보타닉-1은 약 320종의 식물 DNA를 학습한 전문 모델이다. 특정 DNA 서열이 식물의 진화 과정에서 얼마나 보존됐는지 평가하고, 염기 하나가 바뀌었을 때 생물학적으로 얼마나 큰 영향을 줄 수 있는지 점수화한다.

이를 통해 단순히 특정 변이가 형질과 함께 나타나는지를 확인하는 데 그치지 않고, 실제 기능에 영향을 줄 가능성을 평가할 수 있다.

이 모델은  허깅페이스 를 통해 다운로드할 수 있다. 상업적 이용은 제한되며, 연구 목적으로만 자동 라이선스 동의 후 이용할 수 있다.

Finding the exact DNA that makes crops climate-resilient used to take years of physical breeding.

To speed this up, AI lab Living Models pairs Gemma 4 E4B with BOTANIC-1, a genomic language model. Gemma prepares the genomic data, feeding filtered candidates to BOTANIC-1 to score… pic.twitter.com/7OAX3qPu7V

— Google Gemma (@googlegemma) October 7, 2026

연구진이 공개한 연구 결과에 따르면, 500건이 넘는 실험 검증 식물 유전자 변이를 대상으로 한 평가에서도 보타닉-1은 실제 원인 변이를 후보군 상위 0.1% 안에 포함한 비율이 15.9%로 나타났다. 기존 생물정보학 도구를 기반으로 한 비교 대상의 4.6%보다 높은 수치다. 원인 변이를 상위 1% 안에 포함한 비율도 48.8%로, 기존 분석 방식의 33.9%를 웃돌았다.

이번 연구는 범용 AI 하나에 모든 과학적 분석을 맡기기보다, 각 모델의 강점을 결합하는 접근법을 보여준다. 젬마 4는 분석 계획 수립과 데이터 처리, 도구 실행을 담당하고 보타닉-1은 식물 유전체에 대한 전문 지식을 제공한다.

연구진은 "이 같은 시스템을 클라우드가 아닌 연구실 내부(로컬 환경)에서 구동할 수 있어 민감한 유전체 데이터의 외부 유출 위험을 원천 차단하고 운영 비용을 줄일 수 있다"고 강조했다.

기존에는 유전자 변이가 실제 형질에 영향을 주는지 확인하기 위해 수천개의 식물을 재배하고 여러 세대에 걸쳐 실험해야 하는 경우가 많았다. AI가 후보 변이를 빠르게 좁히면 연구자들은 검증에 필요한 시간과 비용을 줄이고, 기후변화에 강한 작물이나 수확량이 높은 품종을 개발하는 연구를 가속할 수 있을 것으로 보인다.

items.content:
Adobe has published 10 new security advisories to inform customers about roughly 140 vulnerabilities found and patched in its products.

Adobe ColdFusion updates address 32 vulnerabilities, including critical bugs that can be exploited for code execution and privilege escalation.

A significant number of flaws have been patched by Adobe in the Content Credentials SDK. The product received fixes for 30 vulnerabilities, many described as high-severity issues that can lead to a security feature bypass. Some security holes can be exploited to cause a DoS condition.

Adobe patched 18 vulnerabilities in Photoshop, nearly all allowing arbitrary code execution.

In Substance 3D Stager, Adobe fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including many high-severity arbitrary code execution flaws.

Eleven vulnerabilities have been resolved in Adobe Commerce, including several critical issues that can be exploited without authentication to execute code or escalate privileges. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Several vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary code execution have been fixed in each of the following products: FrameMaker, Dimension, Substance 3D Sampler, Substance 3D Designer, and Bridge.

Adobe says it’s not aware of any in-the-wild exploitation. Most advisories have a priority rating of 3, which indicates Adobe does not expect to see these vulnerabilities exploited in attacks. Commerce is the only product with a priority rating of 2 (threat actors have historically targeted Commerce ).

Adobe has been using frontier AI models to hunt for flaws in its own code, which helps explain the higher volume of fixes . However, the company has still credited external researchers for many of the newly patched vulnerabilities.

While AI has helped Adobe find more vulnerabilities in its software, engineers still review, validate, and approve all AI-assisted code changes before deployment.

The rise in discoveries led Adobe to stop publishing security bulletins monthly. The company has moved to a twice-monthly schedule, on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month.

items.title: Machine learning pioneer Michael I. Jordan dismantles AI doom rhetoric as "grand moralizing performance"
items.summary: Michael I. Jordan, described by Science as "the most influential computer scientist," considers warnings about superintelligence pure science fiction. He calls the resignations of young AI researchers a "grand moralizing performance" and companies' demands for regulation "theater
items.content:
Machine learning pioneer Michael I. Jordan dismantles AI doom rhetoric as "grand moralizing performance"

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Michael I. Jordan, described by Science in 2016 as "the most influential computer scientist," calls warnings about existential AI threats pure science fiction. In a wide-ranging interview, he takes aim at doomers, company founders, and naive junior researchers.

Jordan, professor emeritus at UC Berkeley, pushed back hard against AI doom rhetoric in an interview with Libération . The 70-year-old machine learning pioneer now works full-time at Inria, the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology in Paris, where he heads the new "markets and learning" chair. When asked about the summer's AI discourse, he called it "totally frustrating."

Jordan warned about the reckless overuse of the term AI back in 2019 . "I wasn't the only one saying it. It was obvious that it would create the hysteria we're seeing now," he says. "You've seen what happened: AI wasn't enough, so they started talking about AGI, and now it's 'superintelligence'..." Ad

Resignations as "moralizing performance"

Jordan dismisses AI companies' demands for regulation as "theater," a way of saying "Look, we're the good guys" while they "would like to have total control over how they are regulated." Ad

The resignation of young Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon , which sparked a wave of collective hysteria over an "AIpocalypse" scenario in early September, is a textbook example in Jordan's view. Many young employees at these companies "aren't really engineers," he says. "They come from the humanities, philosophy, or other disciplines. They're 25 years old, they're naive, they don't do engineering work, they've never worked at large companies where real products are developed for real people, with discipline."

They "get together, a bit like in Parisian cafés in the 1920s, to talk about these grand science-fiction ideas." When they resign, they know they're going to attract attention. "It allows them to feel virtuous and to be seen as very important figures. They claim to be giving up money, but in reality, they already have their stock options." Jordan sees the whole thing as "a grand moralizing performance that doesn't serve the real objective it claims to pursue. There's a great deal of naiveté here, which goes hand in hand with a certain cynicism..." Ad

Superintelligence belongs in science fiction

"Superintelligence" is "a science-fiction term," Jordan says, "and a large part of the debates I've witnessed belong to the realm of science fiction." Occasionally discussing far-fetched scenarios is fine. "Talking about it behind the scenes, as a science-fiction topic, is fine. But when it becomes the dominant discourse, it's very, very harmful. For technological development, for young people, and for the mindset of countries alike." The term is currently being pushed on the US tech elite by President Trump, who are happy to play along .

Jordan is especially harsh on Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has a track record of making bold claims that don't always hold up . "Geoffrey Hinton has never created a company that offers real services for real people," he says. "Hinton believes that we have figured out how the brain works and that we can reproduce it in silicon; we would therefore be able to copy it as many times as we wanted and, by combining what all these copies learn, we would obtain a kind of exponential growth and, there you have it: superintelligence. None of the steps in this argument is credible. Here, we're in the land of science fiction." Ad

He's slightly more generous toward Yoshua Bengio . "Yoshua is a little different; he takes action and does things that directly focus on safety." Bengio's warnings tend to target shortcomings in current AI technology, such as agent swarms spiraling out of control . Ad

items.title: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
items.content:
LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It thinks before it answers, calls tools, and works through multi-step tasks inside popular agent harnesses. Because only 2B parameters are active per token, each reasoning token is cheap, so you can run agents continuously on your own hardware.

LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on LFM2-24B-A2B and keeps its architecture: 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and an in-place tokenizer expansion doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization. Unlike its predecessor, it is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer.

Pre-training was scaled up from ~17T to ~33T tokens. Mid-training then adds 2T tokens at 32K context, weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text, and 300B tokens at 131K context, weighted toward long-context data. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear throughout both phases. Post-training turns the base model into an agent in five stages:

We evaluated LFM2.5-24B-A2B against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning on 16 benchmarks covering tool use and agentic workflows, knowledge, instruction following, math, and coding. It is the smallest model in the group, yet it is competitive with MoEs with ~50% more total and active parameters.

*All the models were evaluated with vLLM, using each benchmark's recommended generation parameters.

For your app, the strengths are tool use and instruction following. LFM2.5-24B-A2B leads or matches the competition on five of the eight tool-use and agentic benchmarks (AutomationBench, BFCLv4, ToolSandbox, LiveClaw, and τ³-Bench Banking), and on AutomationBench it scores more than three times the next-best model. It also leads on all three instruction-following benchmarks. Larger models keep an edge on knowledge-heavy benchmarks like GPQA Diamond, HLE, and AA-Omniscience, and on coding benchmarks like SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) and SciCode, so pair LFM2.5-24B-A2B with retrieval or web search for knowledge-heavy workloads.

These results make LFM2.5-24B-A2B a strong foundation for agents that need to reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device.

LFM2.5-24B-A2B ships with day-one support across the inference ecosystem, including llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX.

Edge inference. LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest of the compared MoEs, decoding 184 tokens/s on an M5 Max and 114 tokens/s on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395. That is up to 1.7x faster than the next-best model, while using the least memory.

GPU inference. LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest model in its size class, reaching over 21K output tokens per second at high concurrency on a single B300.

Reach for LFM2.5-24B-A2B when you need agents that reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device.

items.title: Google Partially Reverses Chrome Bug Bounty Cuts
items.summary: Google is restructuring bug bounty rewards with a focus on complex memory safety vulnerabilities. The post Google Partially Reverses Chrome Bug Bounty Cuts appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Google announced Tuesday that it’s raising bug bounty rewards for some Chrome vulnerabilities, focusing on memory safety issues.

AI has been changing the pace and profile of vulnerability discovery, and the tech giant has been adjusting its bug bounty programs in recent months.

Google significantly lowered standard payout amounts for some Chrome vulnerabilities in April to shift focus to actionable reports, with researchers noting that some rewards became 10 times smaller. At the time it announced a base reward of $500 for memory safety issues, with multipliers for reachability and the level of exploitability.

The company is now quadrupling base rates for memory safety flaws, to $2,000. Despite the increase, the new rates remain well below those offered before the April overhaul.

Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.

V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.

Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.

The company noted that “any submissions that are currently in our evaluation queue submitted after April 30th, 2026 will be evaluated and rewarded under the new payout rules.”

Google recently announced it’s temporarily closing its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) to product vulnerability submissions, prompted by a growing number of AI-generated reports.

items.summary: Google is making it easier to build and use personal Android apps created with AI, without having to make them available to everyone on the Play Store.
items.content:

Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.

These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.

The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.

Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.

These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android.

Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up.

“That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”

In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store.

And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews.

Related to AI’s impact on app development, Google said it’s also building better ways to curate the Google Play experience — for instance, by leveraging Google’s AI to create a personalized game recommendation engine, called Game Finder. The feature, first available in the U.S. in English, will be based on what the user likes to play combined with Google’s knowledge derived from its game community’s 1.2 billion players.

Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates.

Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.

The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience.

■ 노타(대표 채명수)는 14일부터 16일까지 일산 킨텍스에서 열리는 '2026 한국건설·안전박람회'에 참가한다고 밝혔다. 이번 박람회에서는 서버 구축 비용을 최대 85%까지 낮출 수 있는 비전언어모델(VLM) 기반 AI 영상관제 솔루션 '노타 비전 에이전트'를 선보인다. 해당 솔루션은 산업안전, 지능형 교통체계(ITS), 선별관제 등 다양한 분야에 활용되고 있다.

items.content:
TFG London cyberattack disrupts systems at Hobbs and Whistles retailers

TFG London detected a cybersecurity incident that impacted IT systems used by the Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles premium fashion brands.

The company disclosed earlier today that several IT systems remain unavailable, although physical stores remain open for customers.

According to the press release, the incident has not affected the group’s other brands, Inside Story and White Stuff, or its operations in Australia and Africa.

TFG London is the UK subsidiary of South Africa’s The Foschini Group, which owns the aforementioned five fashion and homeware brands.

As of mid-2026, the group operated 649 retail locations globally and reported annual sales of £488 million ($646M).

The company said it detected the cyberattack on October 11 and immediately activated its incident response and business continuity plans, bringing in external cybersecurity experts to help contain the threat.

TFG London is investigating whether any customer information has been compromised, and says it will notify affected individuals or organizations if it data has been affected.

BleepingComputer could not find any threat actor publicly claiming the TFG London breach.

The incident at TFG London comes shortly after another UK fashion retailer, ASOS, suffered a data breach after hackers sent push notifications to users of its mobile app.

The company later confirmed that attackers used social engineering to steal an employee’s login credentials and gained unauthorized access to customer data , including names, contact details, and account information.

At this time, TFG London has not confirmed any customer data exposure, but clients of Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles are advised to remain alert for potential phishing and social engineering attacks.

Earlier this week, rumors emerged about an attack at Swedish multinational clothing company H&M, claimed by an attacker saying they were with the ShinyHunters group and threatening to leak stolen data.

Responding to our request for a comment on these allegations, an H&M spokesperson said they were looking into these claims, although current evidence didn't indicate a breach.

“We are aware of information circulating online regarding a potential cyber security incident and are currently investigating the claims,” the H&M spokesperson told BleepingComputer.

“At this time, we have not found any indications that our data environment has been compromised.”

items.summary: GitHub has taken the step of expiring unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations 48 hours after creation after researchers found that it was possible for an attacker to push new versions of a different user's package without having to steal their credentials. "Your configu
items.content:
GitHub has taken the step of expiring unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations 48 hours after creation after researchers found that it was possible for an attacker to push new versions of a different user's package without having to steal their credentials.

"Your configuration becomes validated and exempt from expiry after its first successful publish," the Microsoft-owned subsidiary said . "Changing the repository or project identity requires a new trust relationship with a fresh 48-hour validation window -- ordinary edits don't restart the deadline."

The change contains the risk associated with trusting a repository or project name that changes ownership, GitHub said, adding npm also rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events going forward, along with the Existing pull_request_target restriction.

In an update to its documentation, GitHub states that a newly created trusted publisher configuration must complete its first successful publish within two days, which validates the configuration and binds it to the "repository's immutable identity."

The development comes in response to findings from Bloom Security, which discovered a loophole within npm's trusted publishing to take over thousands of packages and trigger a Shai-Hulud-style cascading supply chain attack. The findings were reported to GitHub on June 6, 2026.

"Imagine this: an attacker compromises a single package. An AI agent on a popular package maintainer's device autonomously pulls it for a project," security researcher Golan Myers said. "That single endpoint is used to push malicious code to the popular package. All the package users are exposed. All because one person with the correct access was exposed."

Trusted publishing was introduced in npm in July 2025 as a credential-free authentication method that allows developers to push npm packages from a CI/CD platform, such as GitHub Actions, using OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens.

When trusted publishing is configured, the developer's CI/CD provider generates a short-lived cryptographic token for a specific workflow run that the npm registry verifies against a pre-authorized configuration .

This eliminates the need to store, rotate, or manually manage long-lived npm secrets, reducing the risk of credential leaks. It also automatically generates provenance attestations for npm packages, allowing users to establish where a package was built and who published it, thereby strengthening software supply chain security.

However, as Bloom Security found, this security architecture suffered from a problem in how it identified that repository, also called a slug (i.e, the combination of the owner or organization and the repository name that's formatted as "owner/repository").

"It records the repository's address, [...] instead of the permanent ID GitHub assigns it, at least until a version is first published from that repository," Myers explained. "It is like a lock that checks the address on the door rather than who owns the house: when the owner moves out, whoever moves in gets the key."

Put differently, the numeric IDs that survive through repository renaming and transfers are carried by GitHub's OIDC tokens, but are completely ignored by npm until the first successful publish from that repository.

This means the trust is anchored to a name as opposed to an immutable repository ID, a loophole that can be abused by claiming abandoned slugs to inherit their trust. For this attack to succeed, the only prerequisite is that the victim's trusted publisher points to a GitHub slug an attacker can claim, and the repository has never been used to publish a version of the package to npm.

items.title: Sandbox vulnerability gives rogue AI agents a path to escape and leak data, research says
items.summary: The new research, published by AI security startup AIR, found that a network filtering flaw in Vercel Sandbox — a tool used to run code in isolated environments — could allow agents to exploit certificate validation processes to transmit data outside approved networks.
items.content:
Image: JSB Co via Unsplash Sandbox vulnerability gives rogue AI agents a path to escape and leak data, research says

Cybersecurity researchers on Monday said they discovered a vulnerability in a widely used AI development sandbox that could allow rogue agents to leak sensitive information by bypassing restrictions designed to keep them isolated.

The new research , published by AI security startup AIR, found that a network filtering flaw in Vercel Sandbox — a tool used to run code in isolated environments — could allow agents to exploit certificate validation processes to transmit data outside approved networks.

“This vulnerability shows that enterprises can have Hugging Face [style] mini incidents with their own agents,” Niv Hoffman, AIR co-founder and CTO, told Recorded Future News in an interview.

“The new contribution our research makes is [showing] that even in the standard hardened sandbox of today, there are still flaws that will make an agent going rogue manage to escape the sandbox and do things in the wild.”

Developers typically use sandboxes to prevent AI agents from accessing unauthorized systems or transmitting sensitive information. Network allowlists restrict communication to approved destinations, preventing agents from connecting to untrusted servers.

AIR researchers found that rogue agents could circumvent those restrictions by exploiting the way servers handle digital certificates. In a scenario demonstrated by the researchers, a specific certificate was designed that could be sent to an approved server and could then trigger a request to an attacker-controlled server, allowing the information to be transmitted without the sandbox ever directly communicating with the unauthorized destination.

“A crafted certificate is all it takes,” the report said. “The wall meant to keep your secrets in has a door, and the agent holds the key.”

“It’s a very hard leak to patch,” Hoffman said. “This sandbox never communicated directly with the attack server… so from the sandbox perspective, everything looked fine.”

Hoffman said his team contacted Vercel about the vulnerability and the company said it needs time to find a patch because “it's unclear for them right now how it's going to be done.”

Vercel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

AIR has not found evidence of any exploitation of the vulnerability in the wild, but can’t rule out whether or not there has been one, Hoffman said, underscoring that the vulnerability in the Vercel sandbox appeared to be longstanding.

The research is important because it shows that an approved server can become an “unwitting courier for stolen credentials,” according to Nic Adams, co-founder and CEO of 0rcus, a cyberkinetics company. “Security has to account for what happens after the first connection.”

She lives in Washington with her husband and three children.

items.title: West African scam compounds raided, more than 100 suspected trafficking victims ‘rescued’
items.summary: More than two dozen people were arrested by police in Ghana and Nigeria as part of a U.K.-hosted operation that also included tech companies.
items.content:
A scam center in Ghana in October 2026. Image: U.S. Department of Justice West African scam compounds raided, more than 100 suspected trafficking victims ‘rescued’

Police in Ghana and Nigeria arrested or detained 28 people and identified more than 100 suspected victims of human trafficking during an international operation targeting scam compounds in West Africa, U.S. and British officials announced Tuesday.

The operation was hosted by Britain’s National Crime Agency (NCA) in London last week. It brought together 15 law enforcement agencies and the same number of tech companies — including Meta, Microsoft and Google — as part of what they called Joint Disruption Week.

In Ghana, authorities raided a compound in Sasaabi, a semi-rural community outside the capital, Accra, arresting 19 people and seizing 303 devices, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. Nigerian authorities made nine further arrests.

The Ghanaian police also identified 117 people whom the department described as trafficking victims and said were “rescued” and now awaiting repatriation to Nigeria, alongside 89 scam victims who had lost an estimated $8.3 million.

“These networks steal savings on one side of the screen, and people’s freedom on the other,” said Matthew Floyd, a deputy assistant director in the FBI’s Criminal Division.

The Department of Justice said the technology companies it worked with removed more than 3.7 million accounts, pages and groups linked to the West African scam centres.

Meta’s Rob Cochrane gave the same figure for Facebook and Instagram alone. The department did not break the total down by company.

“The disrupted schemes included law enforcement impersonation scams, digital ‘arrest’ extortion schemes, cryptocurrency investment fraud (also known as ‘pig butchering’), and a variety of other online fraud operations targeting global victims,” stated the DOJ.

Following the police action in West Africa, officials said more than $11 million in “potentially freezable” funds had been identified, but did not say how much had been frozen or seized. The FBI’s Floyd described identifying assets as “the easy part.”

Nick Sharp, the NCA’s deputy director of fraud, said it was not yet known how many British or American victims the compounds had targeted, as forensic work on seized devices continues.

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said the operation began with information from Meta, which the NCA also credited as playing “a key role in coordinating the event and encouraging broad private sector participation to maximize scam compound disruption.”

Pirro — a former Fox News host and longtime ally of President Donald Trump — said she was “very proud to work with Meta.” She credited all of the participating businesses with having “voluntarily disrupted scam infrastructure” on their platforms, adding: “And thank God for them.”

Her praise for Meta comes as the company faces scrutiny over fraud on its platforms and questions about whether the right incentives exist for the company to properly tackle such fraud.

A Reuters investigation last year, citing internal company documents, reported that Meta projected about 10% of its 2024 revenue, roughly $16 billion, would come from ads linked to scams and banned goods. Meta disputes that figure and says scams undermine the trust its advertising business depends on.

Last November, Sens. Richard Blumenthal, (D-CT) and Josh Hawley  (R-MO) urged the Federal Trade Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether Meta profited from scam advertising and whether enforcement action was warranted.

Other lawmakers have pushed for broader changes. In February, Sens. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Bernie Moreno (R-OH) introduced the bipartisan SCAM Act, which would require social media companies to take “reasonable steps” to verify advertisers and combat fraudulent ads or face action from the FTC and state attorneys general.

items.summary: Most of the affected individuals are Meta employees in the United States and they are being offered credit monitoring services. The post Meta Says Hackers Took Code, Personal Data of 1,500 in GitHub Breach appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them employees in the US, that their personal information was impacted after hackers got into some of the company’s GitHub repositories.

The intrusion was detected a few weeks ago. According to the tech giant, an outside group gained access to the repositories using an employee’s stolen credentials.

Meta’s security team shut down the attackers’ access and brought in GitHub and law enforcement. Notifications to the impacted individuals started going out on Tuesday.

Meta told SecurityWeek that 99% of the data the hackers took was business data, in the form of software code related to some of its products. The remaining 1% was personal data.

That personal data had been added to the repositories by mistake and should not have been there, as storing it on GitHub went against company policy. Meta has not said what types of personal information were involved.

The company also noted that a significant portion of what looked like personal data was actually synthetic or anonymized test data. As a result, the attackers may not readily be able to tell genuine records apart from test data. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Based on its investigation with GitHub so far, Meta does not believe the hackers were specifically after its data.

Meta is also notifying regulators, and the people whose information was involved are being offered credit and dark web monitoring services.

“This was not a vulnerability in any Meta product, and Meta’s internal systems were not breached. Meta business data held in a GitHub repository was improperly accessed using an employee’s stolen credentials – this included a small amount of personal data for a limited number of people, most of whom were Meta employees,” a Meta spokesperson told SecurityWeek .

In response to the incident, Meta rotated secrets it found in the affected repositories. It also hardened its product security to address risks stemming from access to its business data.

The company is working with its teams that use GitHub to keep user data off the platform. As a second line of defense, it is adding controls for proactive scanning to detect any user data uploaded by mistake.

“We’ve since rotated secrets found in the repositories, implemented new controls to prevent user data from being stored in GitHub, and worked with GitHub on additional measures to protect our repositories,” the spokesperson said.

items.summary: Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway. [...]
items.content:
Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks

Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway.

Formerly known as Pulse Connect Secure and originally Juniper Pulse, the enterprise-grade ICS SSL VPN provides remote employees, contractors, and hybrid workforces with secure access to corporate and cloud resources.

Tracked as CVE-2026-104935 , this high-severity authentication bypass zero-day affects ICS versions 22.8R2.4 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 25.1.1.1 and earlier.

Remote threat actors without privileges can exploit CVE-2026-104935 in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction to execute arbitrary commands on targeted ICS appliances.

"At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild. We are working directly with those organizations while making information, updates and remediation available to the broader customer community. If you are running one of the impacted versions, Ivanti recommends you act immediately," Ivanti said .

"Customers should review the security advisory, upgrade to the fixed version as soon as possible, and run the Integrity Checker Tool regularly."

Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 5,500 ICS instances exposed online , but there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been secured against ongoing attacks.

Internet-exposed ICS instances (Shadowserver)

Cybersecurity firm Volexity, which found and reported the flaw, revealed earlier today that a previously unknown threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 has chained the CVE-2026-104935 vulnerability since at least October 3 with two other flaws to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched devices.

"Notably, UTA0576 deployed no malware or web shell. Instead, the threat actor re-exploited the device for every command it ran and tampered with logs to cover its tracks, evading Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool,"  Volexity said .

While Ivanti has patched two flaws, it is still working to address a privilege escalation vulnerability that UTA0576 exploited as part of the same chain.

Threat intelligence company Defused also confirmed Volexity's report , saying that it caught the first signs of CVE-2026-104935 exploitation in the wild starting October 1.

​Hackers have frequently exploited Ivanti vulnerabilities, often as zero-days, because they provide a quick way to breach enterprise networks and steal sensitive customer and corporate data.

Ivanti has also patched several other Connect Secure zero-days exploited in the wild over the past several years, some of them chained in widespread attacks to deploy malware .

It addressed an authentication bypass (CVE-2023-46805) and a command injection (CVE-2024-21887) in early January 2024 , and a server-side request forgery (CVE-2024-21893) two weeks later .

More recently, it fixed a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability tracked as CVE-2025-0282 in January 2025 and a second RCE flaw (CVE-2025-22457) that China-linked cyber spies have exploited since at least mid-March 2025 .

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged 36 vulnerabilities across various Ivanti products as actively exploited in the wild since November 2021, 12 of which ransomware gangs have also abused.

Ivanti has over 3,000 employees, a network of over 7,000 partners, and more than 40,000 customers worldwide using its IT asset management solutions.

items.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
items.summary: Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user's container repositories using a personal access token (PAT). [...]
items.content:
Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images

Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user’s container repositories using a personal access token (PAT).

Docker Hub is an online registry for storing, sharing, and downloading container images - templates that package everything needed for an application to run in an isolated environment.

In Docker Hub, a PAT serves as a secret used to authenticate tools and workflows. It allows you to pull, push, or delete container images.

According to a security bulletin from the Docker team, an attacker could create an account and PAT, then convert the account into an organization and name a target user as its owner.

The CVE-2026-105445 flaw stems from Docker Hub reassigning a personal access token (PAT) to a designated organization owner without changing its secret or obtaining the target's consent. This allowed the attacker to use the token to authenticate as the target.

Depending on the token’s scope and the target’s permissions, attackers could pull, push, or delete images in the target’s repositories and accessible organizations.

“Within the scope of the token, a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level, meaning an attacker could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images in the target’s repositories and in organizations where the target had access,” Docker explained .

“Because that includes publishing images under a legitimate name, we treated this as a software supply chain risk and rated it critical.”

Although the flaw is critical, Docker noted that it did not provide Docker Hub web access or allow attackers to change passwords, email addresses, or two-factor settings, potentially locking legitimate account holders out.

The vulnerability was introduced on August 26, 2024, when the conversion started reassigning the personal account PAT to the new owner. This occurred without revoking or rotating the secret, and without asking the named owner to confirm the change.

On September 30, 2026, Docker received a vulnerability report describing the issue, confirmed it, and deployed a fix to production less than four hours later.

Docker says it found no evidence of exploitation after examining 304,000 pushes made with transferred tokens and analyzing high-risk public images.

Affected users and organization owners were notified on October 2, and transferred PATs were deactivated on October 8, except for those whose owners explicitly requested to retain them.

Docker says users who didn’t receive a notification should assume they were not impacted and did not need to take any action.

The platform no longer transfers PATs during conversion and requests user consent before naming them an organization owner.

items.title: North Korean hackers target Ukrainian experts for possible intelligence on Russia's war
items.summary: North Korean hackers have been targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security and international policy amid Pyongyang’s growing military cooperation with Russia.
items.content:
Image: Dmitry Ivanov / Wikimedia Commons North Korean hackers target Ukrainian experts for possible intelligence on Russia's war

North Korean hackers have been targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security and international policy amid Pyongyang’s growing military cooperation with Russia, according to a new report.

As part of the campaign, the hacking group Kimsuky used fake conference invitations, research collaboration requests and malicious documents designed to steal information, South Korean cybersecurity firm Genians said in a report published Monday.

North Korea has provided troops to fight in the war in Ukraine as well as other military support to Russia since 2024.

"Kimsuky’s attacks against Ukraine may be aimed at collecting information on the war, the extent of North Korean troop losses, developments in the questioning and handling of prisoners of war, and the details of consultations between South Korea and Ukraine,” researchers said, adding that most of the observed attacks were unsuccessful.

Genians said the transfer of two North Korean soldiers captured by Ukrainian forces to South Korea in September could also be of intelligence interest to Pyongyang, particularly what the prisoners might disclose about North Korean military operations and casualties.

In one attack in August, the hackers impersonated organizers of a cybersecurity conference in Seoul and invited a Ukrainian security expert to speak at the event.

The email included genuine details about the conference and offered to cover travel and accommodation expenses. It initially did not contain malicious links or attachments. Instead, the attackers encouraged the recipient to respond before sending additional materials.

In another case, the hackers posed as a European policy researcher seeking feedback on a report about military cooperation between Russia and North Korea. After the recipient responded, the attackers sent a link to a malicious archive disguised as research material, according to Genians.

The hackers also used files disguised as PDF documents and legitimate Zoom installers to trick recipients into running malicious software. The malware was designed to collect information from infected computers, maintain access to compromised systems and send stolen information to infrastructure controlled by the attackers.

Researchers also identified Japanese-language documents on infrastructure associated with the campaign, suggesting the hackers may have been preparing attacks against Japanese-speaking targets.

These attacks are part of a broader cyberespionage campaign tracked as Operation GitPower, which uses legitimate software development platforms, including GitHub, GitLab and Codeberg, to distribute malicious files and communicate with compromised systems, researchers said.

Kimsuky has been active since at least 2012, targeting governments, think tanks, academics, and media organizations across Asia, Europe, Japan, Russia and the United States. In 2023, the U.S. and its Pacific allies imposed sanctions on the group, accusing it of collecting intelligence to support North Korea’s foreign policy and sanctions-evasion efforts.

In May 2025, cybersecurity firm Proofpoint reported that a North Korean-linked group tracked as TA406 had been sending malicious emails to Ukrainian government agencies, potentially seeking intelligence about the risks facing North Korean troops fighting alongside Russian forces.

According to Proofpoint, TA406’s cyber operations in Ukraine focus on political intelligence and strategic analysis of the war, in contrast to Russian hackers, who typically seek tactical intelligence related to battlefield operations.
